## Goal

As a build agent, I want failing-first regression tests that pin the environment-bound cache contract, so the implementation in the sibling children cannot silently keep serving a drifted-worktree verdict to a canonical-checkout consumer.

## Background

Parent SA-0MVCTZRZD004CE3L (producer decisions Q1c / Q2a / Q3a). Today the cache key is `normalized command + git fingerprint (+ test_type namespace)` only; `store()` records just `interpreter` as environment provenance, so an entry recorded in a worktree with an unpopulated submodule, a differently-resolved `node_modules`, or a different interpreter is key-identical to a canonical-checkout run of the same tree. These tests are written **first** (TDD): they fail against `dev` HEAD and must pass once `skill/test_cache.py` folds a coarse environment fingerprint into the key.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Tests in `tests/test_test_cache.py` (new cases, existing fixture style) fail against today's environment-blind key and pass once the environment fingerprint is keyed: (a) an entry stored under a drifted environment fingerprint is a **miss** for a lookup carrying the canonical environment fingerprint — the verdict is never served; (b) two checkouts with **equivalent** environments share one cache entry (same submodule completeness, same installed `node_modules` state — a symlinked `node_modules` pointing at an identical install counts as equivalent — same interpreter); (c) identical environment state in two different absolute directories yields the **same** environment fingerprint (path-independence).
- Tests assert every stored entry records `environment_fingerprint` plus a human-readable descriptor of its components (submodule status, `node_modules` resolution state, interpreter), and that `lookup()` rejects an entry that predates the field (fail closed — never environment-blind green).
- Tests assert the environment fingerprint is deterministic (two successive computations on an unchanged checkout are byte-identical) and cheap: a spy/monkeypatch proves no recursive `node_modules` walk and at most one `git submodule status` call per computation.
- Existing cache provenance tests (`fingerprint_kind`, `scope`, `test_type`, `interpreter`) keep passing unchanged, and the whole file stays hermetic (temporary git repos, no network, no dependence on the host's installed packages).
- Parent AC6 restated — Regression tests in `tests/` where the cache layer and gates are tested: (a) drift-keyed entries are never served to a canonical-environment consumer — the canonical lookup misses and executes; (b) equivalent-environment entries still share across checkouts (finish gate ↔ pre-push ↔ audit); (c) the escalation path runs `--scope changed --force` for narrow changes and `--scope full --force` on detected drift/refactor; (d) existing cache provenance tests stay green. (This child delivers the cache-layer half (a), (b), (d); the gate-path case is delivered by `run_tests env-aware cache keys and gate provenance`, the escalation case (c) by `finish: escalate post-push verification in canonical env`, and the cross-consumer case (b) end-to-end by `Cross-consumer env-key equivalence and audit evidence notes`; this child owns the failing-first tests those children make pass.)

## Minimal implementation

- Add the new cases to `tests/test_test_cache.py` against the intended API (`compute_environment_state(cwd)`, `cache_key(..., environment_fingerprint=...)`, `store(..., environment=...)`, `lookup(..., environment_fingerprint=...)`).
- Use temporary git repositories plus a synthetic `node_modules/.package-lock.json` marker so drift/equivalence are simulated without touching the real checkout.
- Mark the drift/equivalence cases to fail cleanly (no import error masquerading as a pass) while the primitive does not yet exist.

**Key Files:**

- `tests/test_test_cache.py`
- `skill/test_cache.py` (test target only — no production change in this child)

## Dependencies

- None (first child; every implementation child depends on it).

## Notes / assumptions

- TDD ordering is deliberate: this child lands the failing tests, `test_cache environment fingerprint and provenance` makes them pass.

# Problem

`skill/report/scripts/render_report.py` derives the Conclusion verdict from the
**session's own** acceptance criteria only (`_derive_session_status()` at
`render_report.py:430-440`, called at `render_report.py:540`): all session ACs
`met` ⇒ `status = "completed"` ⇒ the Conclusion prints `✅ Ready to ship`
(`render_report.py:608-612`). The renderer already *knows* the audited work
item's verdict — `_audit_verdict()` (`render_report.py:344-371`) drives the
Meta-Data `Audit:` line and correctly reports `❌ failed` — but that knowledge
never reaches the Conclusion.

Result: an audit session whose work item's audit **failed** still ends with
`✅ Ready to ship` in the report, i.e. in the agent's final message to the
operator. Reported by the operator on 2026-11-16 after an audit run.

**Invariant to enforce: `✅ Ready to ship` may only be rendered when the audit
passed** (`auditResult.readyToClose == true`, equivalently the persisted
`Ready to close: Yes`).

# Live evidence (2026-11-16)

Audit session for `AH-0MWHU5AV800969NA` (Update Hangar War time budget: 5-15
minutes per hex, AI_Hell project). The persisted audit is `Ready to close: No`
(`auditResult.readyToClose: false`, auditedAt 2026-11-16T00:12:36Z). The
rendered report contained, in the same document:

```
## Meta-Data
...
- **Audit:** ❌ failed

## Conclusion

✅ Ready to ship
This completes the audit process for AH-0MWHU5AV800969NA (Update Hangar War time budget: 5-15 minutes per hex).
```

Reproduce with (from any checkout of this repo, project worklog auto-resolved):

```bash
python3 skill/report/scripts/render_report.py AH-0MWHU5AV800969NA \
  --skill-name audit --headline "..." \
  --ac "Work item assessed against acceptance criteria|audit report|met" \
  --ac "Audit verdict determined and recorded|Ready to close line|met" \
  --ac "Ready-to-close line added|persisted audit report|met"
```

Operator impact: the last lines of a session — the part a producer actually
reads — can authorise shipping work whose audit failed. The Meta-Data line is
correct but sits far above the verdict and is easy to miss.

# Desired behaviour

1. When the report is rendered by the **audit** skill (`--skill-name audit`,
   case-insensitive), the Conclusion verdict is gated on the resolved audit
   verdict (`_audit_verdict(work_item, audit_result)`), in addition to the
   session ACs:
   - audit `yes` + every session AC `met` ⇒ `✅ Ready to ship` (today's text);
   - audit `no` ⇒ `🚫 Not ready to ship`, plus one reason line naming the
     verdict and the exact command to read the persisted report, e.g.
     `Audit verdict: Ready to close: No — see \`wl audit-show <id> --json\`.`;
   - audit `unknown` (no stored audit at all) ⇒ **not** ready (fail closed),
     reason line `Audit verdict: not run — no persisted audit for <id>.`
2. The header line (`# {status.title()} {skill_name}`) must agree with the
   Conclusion: no `# Completed audit` over a `🚫 Not ready to ship` verdict
   (it becomes `# Incomplete audit`, deriving from the gated status).
3. Both entry points apply the rule identically: the `wl`-backed path
   (`render_from_wl`, `render_report.py:688-730`, already forwards
   `audit_result=data.get("auditResult")`) and the `--json` stdin path
   (`render_report_from_workitem`).
4. **Non-audit skills are unchanged** — `implement`, `plan`, `intake`, `test`,
   `refactor`, … byte-identical output to before this change (they have no
   audit verdict to consult and must not start failing closed).
5. No new `wl` calls: the verdict must come from data already fetched
   (`workItem.auditResult` / top-level `auditResult` / legacy `workItem.audit`).

# Key files

- `skill/report/scripts/render_report.py` — `_derive_session_status` (gate it),
  `render_report` (`:483-630`), `render_report_from_workitem`, `render_from_wl`,
  `_audit_verdict` (`:344`), `AUDIT_ICONS`.
- `skill/report/tests/` — the verdict-matrix regression tests.
- `skill/report/SKILL.md` — document the invariant in the Conclusion section.
- `skill/audit/SKILL.md` — its "Final step: standardized end-of-session
  report" note currently explains that the Conclusion records the *session's*
  success; it must state that a failed audit now forces `🚫 Not ready to ship`
  (keep the two docs consistent).
- `skill/shared/herdr_pane.py` (`derive_status`) — see Risks; read-only unless
  the pane surface is fixed in the same change.

# Acceptance criteria

1. Rendering an **audit** report for a work item whose stored audit is
   `readyToClose: false` produces `🚫 Not ready to ship`, contains **no**
   `✅ Ready to ship` / `Ready to ship` success claim, and includes a reason
   line naming the audit verdict (a test asserts this over the real
   `AH-0MWHU5AV800969NA`-shaped payload: audit `no` + all session ACs `met`).
2. Rendering an **audit** report for a work item whose stored audit is
   `readyToClose: true` still produces `✅ Ready to ship` (no regression to the
   passing case).
3. Rendering an **audit** report for a work item with **no** stored audit
   (`auditResult` absent/null and no legacy `workItem.audit`) produces
   `🚫 Not ready to ship` with an "audit not run" reason (fail closed).
4. The header line and the Conclusion never disagree: `completed` ⇒
   `✅ Ready to ship`, `incomplete` ⇒ `🚫 Not ready to ship`, for all three audit
   verdict states and for both session-AC states (matrix test).
5. The rule is applied identically on both entry points: a test renders the
   same fixture through the `--json` stdin path and through `render_from_wl`
   (with `wl show` mocked) and asserts the same verdict line.
6. Non-audit skills are unaffected: a regression test renders an `implement`
   report with an `auditResult.readyToClose: false` payload and asserts the
   output is unchanged (still `✅ Ready to ship` when its own ACs are met).
7. `skill/report/SKILL.md` states the invariant ("`Ready to ship` in the
   Conclusion implies the audit passed; a failed or missing audit renders
   `Not ready to ship`") and `skill/audit/SKILL.md`'s final-step note is
   updated to match.
8. New/updated tests pass through the test skill (`/skill:test`) and the full
   project test suite is green.

# Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** the audit verdict is authoritative for the audit skill's
  Conclusion; the session ACs (audit was performed) remain the only input for
  every other skill. This matches the operator's report: *"If it is ready to
  ship the audit must have passed."*
- **Related surface (consider, not required):** `apply_pane_status()` /
  `skill/shared/herdr_pane.derive_status()` derive the herdr pane title from
  the same session ACs, so a failed audit can also show a success pane status.
  Out of scope here unless it is a one-line follow-on; file separately if not.
- **Scope creep risk:** the `Ready to ship` wording is also produced for
  release/ship sessions; those legitimately claim shipping readiness and must
  keep today's behaviour (AC6 pins this).

# Related work

- `discovered-from:AH-0MWHU5AV800969NA` (AI_Hell) — the audit session that
  surfaced this: verdict `Ready to close: No`, rendered Conclusion
  `✅ Ready to ship`.
- `SA-0MVQ1QKLN007S1BW` / `SA-0MVQ1QL5G007MLGM` — shared routine-next-step
  classifier and pane-status derivation that `apply_pane_status` consumes.
- `SA-0MTQY7YM5009J6QR` — the change that made the audit skill render its
  report through this renderer with session-level ACs (the origin of the
  split between "session succeeded" and "audit passed").
- `SA-0MVYEZ3V3004AQXN` — clearer audit results (Conclusion verdict line).
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **SA-0MSRFPUTN0089F3U** – Write tests for report renderer (completed)
- **SA-0MSYYCTPV004MVB1** – fix: render_report.py doesn't handle 'adjusted'/'partial' AC verdicts (completed)
- **SA-0MVYEZ3V3004AQXN** – Clearer audit results (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — matched: 36z, absent, ac6, acceptance, acs (+234 more)
- `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` — matched: absent, ac6, acceptance, acs, actually (+229 more)
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` — matched: 36z, absent, ac6, acceptance, acs (+222 more)

# Impact

An audit report now ends with `🚫 Not ready to ship` (plus a reason line) whenever the audit failed or was never run, so the operator is never told that failed work is ready to ship.

# Intake Brief: Do not require repeated producer reviews during release

## Problem statement

When a release re-audits work items (gate remediation, freshness re-runs), the
items are sometimes re-armed with `needsProducerReview`, so the producer is
asked to re-approve work the release itself has just touched. The desired rule
is simple: **require a producer review only when the audit failed for any
reason, or when code/content changed since the last review** — never because a
passing re-audit of unchanged work ran during a release.

## Users

- **Producer (operator)** — user story: "When I run a release I don't want the
  release's own re-audits to put passing, unchanged items back into my review
  queue; I only want to see genuine failures or actual changes."
- **Release engineer / automated release agent** — user story: "I want the
  producer-review flag to mean exactly 'the producer must look now', so the
  release gate neither blocks on already-reviewed unchanged work nor silently
  lets a failed item drop off the queue."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Producer-review policy is stated and enforced.** `needsProducerReview` is
   set only when (a) the audit failed for any reason (an independent or
   ship-triggered verdict of `Ready to close: No`), or (b) the item's audited
   content/code changed since the last producer review. A passing re-audit of
   unchanged work — including during a release — never sets it.
2. **Failed ship-triggered re-audits still surface to the producer.** A
   ship-gate re-audit (SA-0MW92TODX00064XQ's shipped `--ship-triggered` path)
   whose verdict is `Ready to close: No` still sets `needsProducerReview` for
   the item to reach the producer queue; the ship-triggered carve-out
   suppresses only the passing/verification case. Where this diverges from
   SA-0MW92TODX00064XQ AC1 ('No' verdict leaves the flag untouched), the
   producer's stated rule in this item takes precedence and the divergence is
   reconciled (that item's Appendix Q2 explicitly awaited producer
   confirmation, which this item provides).
3. **Code/content-change trigger is not swallowed.** The ship-triggered
   suppression never overrides the content-fingerprint change signal: a
   ship-triggered re-audit of an item whose audited content changed since the
   last review still resolves to `required`, exactly as an independent audit
   would.
4. **Targeted tests.** Tests exercise production code and lock: passing
   unchanged re-audit → no flag write; failed re-audit (independent and
   ship-triggered) → flag write; content change → flag write; marker absence
   → flag behaviour unchanged.
5. **Documentation updated.** `skill/audit/SKILL.md`,
   `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` and
   `skill/ship/docs/dev/ship-skill-reference.md` document the
   only-when-failed-or-changed flag rule and the ship-triggered carve-out
   boundary (passing suppressed, failing/change still flagged).
6. **Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Impact

Producers stop being asked to re-review work the release simply re-audited,
while genuine audit failures and real changes still land in their queue.

## Constraints

- **Independent audit behaviour unchanged.** Audits run outside release
  automation keep today's flag rules exactly (SA-0MVR9B1UH002BUST,
  SA-0MVZNECSD005XB42, SA-0MSSVKYEW008PJ9H preserve/required/untouched
  semantics); only ship-automated verification runs are touched.
- **No new flag-clearing behaviour.** Suppression means "don't write the
  flag", never `--needs-producer-review no` retro-clearing; the ship close
  step's authorised override (SA-0MUJLWPB10038Z8Q) is unchanged.
- **Reconcile with SA-0MW92TODX00064XQ before/while implementing.** That item
  is already planned (plan_complete); its 'No'-verdict suppression must be
  reconciled with AC2 of this item rather than silently shipping both.
- **Repository boundary.** Changes live in SorraAgents skills (audit, ship)
  and their docs; no herdr/ContextHub change required.

## Existing state

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — `_resolve_producer_review_decision()`
  (~line 2978) resolves `preserved`/`required`/`untouched`;
  `_passing_audit_producer_decision()` (~line 2907) mirrors the passing
  verdict; `_apply_terminal_lifecycle()` (~line 17741) writes
  `--needs-producer-review yes` when `required`. The blanket ship-triggered
  short-circuit sits at ~line 3041 and covers **both** `Yes` and `No` today.
  Existing carve-outs: child items never flagged; cascade-demotion-suppressed
  'No' untouched; tracked/accepted medium/low candidate-false-positive chores
  untouched; tainted/infrastructure-failure verdicts untouched.
- `skill/ship/scripts/check-audit-gate.js` (~line 953),
  `check-final-validation.js` (~line 480), `refresh-audits.js` (~line 132) —
  release-gate re-audit call sites that now run
  `audit_runner.py issue <id> --strict --ship-triggered` (SA-0MW92TODX00064XQ
  is **completed**: marker plumbing landed via SA-0MWJ7K962006646G and
  SA-0MWJ7KPC00073EMP, so this item reconciles shipped behaviour rather than a
  planned mechanism).
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_producer_review.py` — ships
  `TestShipTriggeredReviewDecision` (~lines 665–711), which pins today's
  blanket suppression; its 'No'-verdict assertion is the one this item
  deliberately supersedes.
- Flag-rule precedents: SA-0MVR9B1UH002BUST (preserve review across passing
  re-audits, flag independent failures), SA-0MS1WXHVF008AKQW (flag when
  automated audit says ready to close), SA-0MSSVKYEW008PJ9H (top-level only).

## Desired change

- Confirm the producer-review flag rule as stated in AC1 and enforce it in the
  audit runner and the release flow: passing re-audits of unchanged items never
  set the flag; failing re-audits and content/code changes always do.
- Reconcile with SA-0MW92TODX00064XQ: its ship-triggered marker suppression
  covers the passing/verification case only; the failing-verdict case keeps
  flagging (or the divergence is explicitly recorded and producer-approved).

## Key Files

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — `_resolve_producer_review_decision()`
  and `_passing_audit_producer_decision()`: enforce only-when-failed-or-changed;
  ship-triggered marker consultation must not swallow failure/change signals.
- `skill/ship/scripts/check-audit-gate.js`, `check-final-validation.js`,
  `refresh-audits.js` — reconciliation with SA-0MW92TODX00064XQ marker
  threading (failing-verdict boundary).
- `skill/audit/SKILL.md`, `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md`,
  `skill/ship/docs/dev/ship-skill-reference.md` — document the flag rule and
  the carve-out boundary.
- `skill/audit/tests/` (`test_audit_runner_producer_review.py`,
  `test_audit_runner_lifecycle.py`) — AC4 coverage.

## Related work

- **SA-0MW92TODX00064XQ** — Ship skill triggered audits should not mark for
  producer review (completed, done; marker children SA-0MWJ7K962006646G and
  SA-0MWJ7KPC00073EMP completed): the shipped ship-triggered marker mechanism
  this item's rule constrains; reconciliation performed by AC2/AC3.
- **SA-0MVR9B1UH002BUST** — Audit runner: preserve a producer's review across
  passing re-audits; flag failing audits (completed): defines the
  preserved/required/untouched decision the release rule extends.
- **SA-0MS1WXHVF008AKQW** — Set producerReview flag when automated audit marks
  item as ready to close (completed): the foundational flag-on-yes rule.
- **SA-0MSSVKYEW008PJ9H** — Audit pass should set needsProducerReview only for
  top-level items (completed): child carve-out.
- **SA-0MVZNECSD005XB42** — audit_runner sets needsProducerReview for every
  medium/low CFP chore (completed): CFP carve-out (same suppression spirit).
- **SA-0MUJLWPB10038Z8Q** — Ship skill: release-ready parent must override or
  absorb needsProducerReview on children (completed): close-step override kept
  out of scope here.
- **SA-0MVX4EHUP0042V9G** — Ship skill invalidates audits (open): adjacent
  freshness concern, distinct ACs.
- Potentially related docs: `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md`
  (Producer-review flag lifecycle ~lines 444–542), `skill/audit/SKILL.md`,
  `skill/ship/docs/dev/ship-skill-reference.md`.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk — contradictory ACs between items.** SA-0MW92TODX00064XQ's planned
  AC1 suppresses the flag for ship-triggered 'No' verdicts; AC2 of this item
  requires a failing ship-triggered re-audit to flag. Mitigation: this item
  records Blocked-by (SA-0MW92TODX00064XQ) and the reconciliation is made
  explicit before either is implemented; if the producer prefers the
  SA-0MW92TODX00064XQ behaviour, AC2 is amended via that item's plan, not
  silently.
- **Risk — marker leakage** (from SA-0MW92TODX00064XQ): the ship-triggered
  marker must not be settable in an operator's shell. Mitigation: adopt the
  planned CLI-flag mechanism, never an env var.
- **Assumption — 'code was changed' = content-fingerprint change.** The only
  change signal the runner has today is the title/description content
  fingerprint; a repo/commits-change signal is out of scope (separate work
  item if desired).
- **Scope-creep guard.** Verdict semantics, close-step overrides, and the
  freshness/time-gate concerns of SA-0MVX4EHUP0042V9G are deliberately out of
  scope; they remain linked work items.

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- **OPEN QUESTION (failing ship-triggered re-audit):** Should a ship-gate
  re-audit whose verdict is `Ready to close: No` still set
  `needsProducerReview`, or is demotion out of the release queue sufficient (as

## Summary

Resolve every implement-session path from one canonical root computation and fail fast
with the exact paths when the worktree, checkout or item prefix does not match.

## Problem

Log review shows repeated `cd` failures, reads against the main checkout while a
worktree was expected, and risky git calls on the wrong tree. `implement.py` resolves
paths in several places (`Path.cwd()`, ad-hoc `git rev-parse`, `worktree_path_for`,
`IMPLEMENT_WORKTREE_PATH`), so a session can silently operate on the wrong root —
exactly the failure the worktree-isolation invariant exists to prevent.

## Users

- AI agents: need a single command that prints the roots they must use, before any edit.
- Reviewers: need a fail-closed error naming both the expected and the actual root.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `implement.py` commands resolve and validate the canonical worktree root before any git operation, through one helper used by every phase.
- `resolve_session_roots(work_item_id, worktree_path)` returns `repo_root`, `worktree_root`, `main_checkout_root` and `git_dir`, honouring the documented precedence (`--worktree-path` / `IMPLEMENT_WORKTREE_PATH` / worklog-derived default) in one place.
- A read-only `roots` action prints those values (`--json` supported) so an agent can verify the root before writing; the implement skill instructs agents to run it first.
- Commands exit 2 with an actionable message naming the expected and resolved paths when the worktree is missing, is not a linked worktree, its `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` differs from the expected root, or the item prefix belongs to another project.
- Behaviour is unchanged when launched from the owning checkout, and a worktree launch never resolves git to the main checkout.
- The worktree-root resolution tests cover main-checkout launch, worktree launch, nested/dirty cwd, missing worktree and foreign-prefix item.

## Minimal Implementation

- Tests first: `skill/implement/tests/test_implement_worktree_root_resolution.py` and `test_implement_roots_action.py`, mirroring the defensive-walk style of `skill/shared/tests/test_resolve_repo_root.py`.
- Add `resolve_session_roots(...)` and thread its result through `phase_start`/`phase_finish`/`phase_drive`/`phase_parent` instead of scattered `Path.cwd()` / `git rev-parse` calls.
- Add the read-only `roots` action (no state writes) and reference it from the implement skill's first step and the worktree-isolation doc.
- Add the fail-closed validation with expected/actual path pairs and a one-line remediation hint.
- Document precedence, validation order and the foreign-prefix rule in `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md` and `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md`.

## Key Files

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` (`worktree_path_for`, `git_rev_parse_is_inside_work_tree`, phase functions, `parse_args`)
- `skill/implement/tests/test_implement_worktree_root_resolution.py` (new)
- `skill/implement/tests/test_implement_roots_action.py` (new)
- `skill/shared/tests/test_resolve_repo_root.py` (pattern to mirror)
- `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md`
- `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md`
- `skill/implement/SKILL.md`

- None. This is the foundational item: `SA-0MWJYSYJO009ICNP` (status/heartbeat) and `SA-0MWJYT0RB00697OM` (git recovery) depend on it.

## Risks and assumptions

- Assumption: root resolution can be centralised without changing the documented worktree layout (`.worklog/worktrees/wl-<id>-<slug>`); if a caller relies on the current ad-hoc resolution, its test will surface it.
- Risk: `live_repo_guard` / inherited-index guards are sensitive to cwd and git env; the resolver must not perturb `GIT_DIR`/`GIT_WORK_TREE` handling.
- Prior art: `SA-0MSRMBMPP0035L6S` redirected audit-side git commands to the owning project root; this item applies the same principle to the implement session and adds the CLI surface.

- One resolver plus a read-only `roots` action in `implement.py`.
- Fail-closed validation with exact-path errors in every phase.
- Regression tests for the five launch scenarios and updated isolation docs.

Agents stop guessing which checkout they are in: one command shows the roots and a wrong root now fails immediately with both paths named instead of silently editing the main checkout.

# Release gate treats a red build as non-fatal and never type-checks

## User story

As a producer, I want the dev→main release gate to refuse a tree that does not
build or type-check, so a broken release cannot be published.

## Problem

`skill/ship/scripts/release/merge-dev-to-main.sh` verifies tests, but not types,
and does not treat a failed build as fatal. Two concrete defects:

1. **A red build is a warning, not a block.** The derived-version-file step runs
   the repo's build (`regenerate-version.js`) on the merged tree before tagging,
   but a failure only logs:
   `Warning: derived version file regeneration failed (continuing with release)`
   and the release proceeds (merge-dev-to-main.sh, "Regenerate derived version
   files" block). A tree whose build fails therefore still gets tagged, pushed
   and promoted.

2. **The full-suite gate does not type-check.** The only hard assertion is
   `run_tests.py --scope full --strict-git-env`. Every test runner in the
   framework (vitest, node --test, pytest) transpiles or interprets without
   type-checking, so a TypeScript type error yields a green suite. A repo that
   does not fail its build gate (defect 1) can ship code that does not compile.

Consequence (real incident, ContextHub v1.0.30): merge `485b764c7` resolved
conflicts by dropping code while leaving its consumers in place, producing 9
`TS2305`/`TS2724` errors in `packages/herdr`. The full suite was green, the
build step was non-fatal, and the broken tree was released to `main`.

The `implement.py finish` changed-scope gate has the same blind spot: it runs
tests, and tests do not typecheck.

## Desired change

- Make the release gate's build step **fatal**: a build failure on the merged
  tree blocks the release (exit non-zero before tagging), with an explicit
  documented bypass env var analogous to `SHIP_TEST_SKIP` for genuine
  emergencies.
- Add a build/type-check assertion to the release contract that is independent
  of the derived-version-file regeneration (they serve different purposes, and
  the regeneration step is legitimately non-fatal for *its own* purpose).
- Document the requirement so projects wire a `typecheck`/`build` script that
  covers their full source tree, including package subtrees (a root `tsc` with
  `include: ["src/**/*"]` does not cover `packages/*`).
- Consider surfacing the same check in the `implement.py finish` gate guidance.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A release whose merged tree fails `npm run build` is blocked before tagging
  (verified with a throwaway failing-build commit on a scratch branch).
- The release remains able to complete when the build succeeds.
- Any bypass is explicit, documented and logged (mirroring `SHIP_TEST_SKIP`).
- `docs/dev/release-process.md` / `ship` skill docs describe the build gate and
  state that the full-suite gate does not substitute for type-checking.
- A project whose build does not cover package subtrees is called out in the
  docs as a project-side configuration error, not silently accepted.

## Constraints

- Do not weaken the existing full-suite gate or its cache contract.
- The derived-version-file regeneration step keeps its own non-fatal semantics
  for *regeneration*; only a build *failure* becomes blocking.
- Existing projects without a `build` script must be unaffected.

**Key Files:**

- skill/ship/scripts/release/merge-dev-to-main.sh
- skill/ship/scripts/release/regenerate-version.js
- tests/test_release_full_suite_gate.py
- skill/ship/tests/test_regenerate_version.mjs
- skill/ship/SKILL.md
- docs/dev/release-process.md
- docs/dev/release-tests.md
- docs/dev/ship-skill-reference.md

## Implementation sketch (plan review)

Test-first, single vertical slice (no child items — effort Small / risk Low):

1. **Test first.** Add `tests/test_release_build_gate.py`, mirroring the
   established harness in `tests/test_release_full_suite_gate.py` (throwaway
   repo with `main`/`dev` + bare `origin`, fake `gh`, isolated `HOME`):
   a failing-build fixture asserts a non-zero exit **before any tag exists**;
   a passing-build fixture asserts the release proceeds.
2. **Fatal build gate.** In `merge-dev-to-main.sh`, assert the repo's build
   (`package.json` `scripts.build`) on the merged tree as its own step —
   independent of derived-file regeneration, which keeps its non-fatal
   *regeneration* semantics. Runs after the tree-modifying steps and before
   the tag, alongside the full-suite gate. No `scripts.build` → no-op, so
   repos without a build are unaffected.
3. **Bypass.** Proposed `SHIP_BUILD_SKIP=1`, mirroring `SHIP_TEST_SKIP`:

## Goal

`implement.py parent` / `implement.py drive` must be usable when the repository already contains
uncommitted work in the main checkout or in **other** items' worktrees. Today a child whose worktree is
clean makes the whole chain fail closed before *any* session is spawned, because pre-existing ambient
dirt is attributed to that child.

## User story

As an operator driving an epic, I want `implement.py drive <epic>` to start the next startable child even
when the repo already holds unrelated uncommitted work, so that a long-lived checkout with several items
in flight does not make every epic undriveable.

## Reproduction (established 2026-11-17, `llm` repo, epic LP-0MVVCO1N7004TNGY)

1. Repo with 1+ dirty path in the **main checkout** (here: `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests/conftest.py`,
   `test_gpu_busy.py`) and several **sibling worktrees** holding pre-existing uncommitted changes from other
   items (here: `wl-LP-0MTD4C1HN005I48W-…` `.pi/.../fixtures.py`; `wl-LP-0MVWU8WZU…` `proxy/proxy/provider.py`;
   `wl-LP-0MVWEBY3Y…` `.pi/.../aggregation.py` + `scripts/capacity_signal_verification.py`;
   `wl-LP-0MVZ4R2B2…` `docs/dev/measurement-windows.md`).
2. An epic whose next child (`LP-0MVVXGI490089OX5`) has an existing **clean** worktree with **zero commits
   ahead** of `dev` — i.e. the child has produced no work yet in this run.
3. `python3 skill/implement/scripts/implement.py drive LP-0MVVCO1N7004TNGY`

Observed: `phase_drive` → `parent` subprocess exits non-zero, `Sessions spawned: 0`, and the report contains
one `produced changes in the main checkout …` plus one `produced changes in the sibling worktree …` entry per
dirty surface, each ending with `Move these changes into <child worktree> (or discard them), then re-run.`

Expected: no violation. Nothing in the run wrote those paths; the child's worktree is simply empty because its
session has not started.

## Root cause

`_child_main_checkout_violation()` (`skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`) fires when **all** of:

1. the child is non-terminal,
2. the child's worktree holds no changes (clean, zero commits ahead of the parent branch),
3. any other change surface (main checkout or a registered sibling worktree) holds changes.

Condition 3 has no time component, so **pre-existing** dirt is indistinguishable from a child that strayed.
The only existing exemption is `read_spawn_failure(worktree, child_id)` — a record the **driver** writes after
a spawned child session dies (SA-0MWGZ8NWP009QD8G, SA-0MWGZ86MS005OE61, SA-0MWGZ8E7C001X2HA). That exemption
cannot apply here: the guard fires in the same `phase_parent` call that would have spawned the session, so no
spawn-failure record exists and none ever will.

Net effect: on a checkout with any ambient dirt, `parent`/`drive` are unusable for **every** epic whose next
child has a clean worktree — the common case at the start of a child.

## Proposed fix (design)

Snapshot the foreign change surfaces **before** the run can attribute anything to a child, and compare:

- Option A (preferred): record, once per `phase_drive`/`phase_parent` invocation (or persistently in the
  child's `.implement_state.json` at `start`), the set of dirty paths in the main checkout and in each
  registered sibling worktree, plus each surface's HEAD. A violation is then only reported for paths/commits
  that are **new or changed since the snapshot**.
- Option B: treat a child that has **no session activity at all** (no state-file activity timestamp newer
  than the surface's newest change) as exempt, analogous to the spawn-failure exemption.
- Either way: keep the genuine SA-0MW5FIJNQ002Z24I detection — a child session that writes into the main
  checkout or a sibling worktree after its spawn must still fail closed.

Do not silence the guard through `ignoreDirtyPaths`; the dirt is not "expected", it is another item's
in-flight work.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: A regression test reproduces the exact scenario — dirty main checkout, 1+ dirty sibling worktree, and a
  startable child with an existing clean worktree holding zero commits ahead — and asserts
  `phase_parent` reports the child as startable (`action: implement` / a spawn decision), **not** a placement
  violation.
- AC2: A regression test asserts the genuine case still fails closed: a child session that writes only into the
  main checkout, or only into another item's linked worktree, is still reported as a placement violation even
  when other (pre-existing) dirt is present.
- AC3: `drive` spawns the next startable child in the reproduced scenario (asserted on a fake spawner, no real
  Pi session), and the report no longer lists unrelated sibling worktrees as offenders.
- AC4: The failure message for a genuine violation still names the offending paths and the child's worktree;
  the snapshot/threshold semantics are documented in `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md` and the skill reference.
- AC5: Full suite green at the dev-push gate.

## Evidence

- `llm` epic `LP-0MVVCO1N7004TNGY`; failing log: `.worklog/logs/drive-LP-0MVVCO1N7004TNGY-181554.log`.
- Workaround used by the epic session: spawn each child session directly
  (`pi -p "/skill:implement <child>" --approve --no-extensions` with `IMPLEMENT_DRIVE_ACTIVE=1` and
  `IMPLEMENT_WORKTREE_PATH`), i.e. reimplement the driver loop by hand; the parent is then advanced with a
  final `implement.py parent` once every child is terminal.

## Not in scope

- Cleaning the ambient dirt itself (belongs to the owning items / operator).
- The per-child lock and pane-transport behaviour (unchanged).

## Impact

An operator can drive an epic's next child on a checkout that already holds unrelated in-flight work, instead of every epic becoming undriveable until that dirt is cleaned.

## User story

As an operator auditing a work item whose pushed commit the dev-push gate already failed, I want the audit's **red-entry diagnostics** to read the gate's tree-keyed verdict, so a red gate verdict produces the same structured failure diagnostics as a red loose-key entry today — instead of the verdict being invisible and the audit re-executing the whole suite.

## Scope: the residual gap only (duplicate-work reconciliation)

`SA-0MWB1H4RF006R7SI` ("Audit: reuse the tree-keyed dev-push gate verdict for full-suite evidence", stage `plan_complete`) already owns the green-evidence half of this gap with a four-child decomposition:

- `SA-0MWIXIO0R006HL36` — Core: `_classify_full_suite_cache` tree-first query with worktree fallback
- `SA-0MWIXJOBO001SFK8` — Tests: tree-kind hit / legacy worktree hit / different-tree miss
- `SA-0MWIXJ84T000GBWG` — Reporting: surface `fingerprint_kind` and age in audit output
- `SA-0MWIXK8XW003VA3D` — Docs: test-skill-reference and audit evidence documentation

That item's "Desired change" explicitly places `_cached_red_failures` **out of scope** ("red-diagnostics only; a red entry never satisfies evidence and the caller executes fresh"). That is the uncovered gap this item now covers, and only that gap: the green-evidence acceptance criteria of this item's original description are dropped as owned by `SA-0MWB1H4RF006R7SI`. Re-scoped during planning on 2026-11-17 (see the plan comment for the AC comparison).

## Problem

`.githooks/pre-push` and `implement.py finish` bind their full-suite verdict to the pushed commit's **tree** SHA (`run_tests.py --scope full --fingerprint <tree>` → `fingerprint_kind="tree"`, SA-0MW7C6BMZ00931JG / SA-0MWFJS3820032YB4). `implement.py` reads that entry back tree-first (`_full_suite_cache_present`, added by SA-0MWAXC5TD00461FN).

`_cached_red_failures()` (`skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py:4759`) never does this. It calls:

```python
entry = query_cached(command, cwd=str(root), ttl=AUDIT_CACHE_TTL_SECONDS)
```

with **no** `fingerprint` and **no** `fingerprint_kind`, so it looks up the loose *worktree* key (`sha256(HEAD + dirty content)`, `compute_git_state` in `skill/test_cache.py`) — a different namespace from the tree key.

Consequences:

- A red tree-keyed gate verdict at the audited `HEAD` is **invisible**: no failure records are parsed.
- `_cached_red_evaluation()` therefore returns `None`, and the audit falls back to the execute-dependent path (a fresh suite run) rather than explaining the failure from the evidence the gate already produced.
- The 24 h `AUDIT_CACHE_TTL_SECONDS` acceptance window (SA-0MVECQUGF0064U81) does not reach gate-produced red runs at all.

## Proposed approach

1. Reuse the tree-resolution helper the core child introduces (`_resolve_audited_tree`, per `SA-0MWIXIO0R006HL36`, mirroring `implement.py`'s `_resolve_commit_tree`). Do **not** introduce a second resolver.
2. In `_cached_red_failures()`, resolve the audited `HEAD`'s tree once, then for each full-suite command query **tree-first** — `query_cached(command, cwd=..., ttl=AUDIT_CACHE_TTL_SECONDS, fingerprint=<tree>, fingerprint_kind=FINGERPRINT_KIND_TREE)` — falling back to today's loose-worktree query only on a tree miss (legacy entries).
3. Fail-soft on an unresolvable tree: fall back to the loose query, never raise into the caller (the existing `except Exception` miss contract stays), and never fabricate a failure.
4. Keep the existing filters byte-for-byte: a `scope != "full"` entry is still not red diagnostics (SA-0MT6CEO700058ZEN), and only `exit_code != 0` entries are parsed.
5. Record provenance on each returned failure record (`fingerprint_kind`, plus `tree` when tree-keyed) so a reader can tell a reused gate verdict from a loose-key entry. `_cached_red_evaluation()` consumes the same records — no duplicated lookup logic.
6. Leave `skill/test_cache.py` untouched: `query_cached()`'s worktree-only default (`fingerprint=None`, legacy keying) must stay byte-for-byte for every other caller.

## Acceptance criteria

1. `_cached_red_failures()` consults the tree-keyed entry before the loose worktree key, and a red tree-keyed full-suite entry at the audited `HEAD` yields the same parsed failure records as the identical loose-key entry today.
2. Loose-key fallback is unchanged: a legacy worktree-keyed red entry (with no tree entry) still parses exactly as today.
3. A tree entry recorded for a *different* tree is ignored — a red verdict for another tree is never attributed to the audited `HEAD`.
4. An uncomputable tree (`git rev-parse HEAD^{tree}` failure / detached / corrupt) falls back to the loose query only: no crash, no fabricated failure, no unhandled exception.
5. Red diagnostics still flow through the single path: `_cached_red_evaluation()` obtains them from `_cached_red_failures()`, with no second cache query implementation.
6. Each returned failure record carries machine-readable provenance (`fingerprint_kind`, and `tree` when tree-keyed) so a reused gate verdict is distinguishable from a loose-key entry.
7. Changed-scope (partial) entries remain non-evidence for red diagnostics, exactly as today.
8. `query_cached()`'s worktree-only default is unchanged for every other caller (no signature or default change in `skill/test_cache.py`).
9. Tests, executed through the test skill, cover: tree-keyed red hit, legacy loose-key red hit, different-tree ignored, uncomputable-tree fallback — deterministic (no real cache dir, no live git state; prime a tmp cache / stub `query_cached`). Avoid the `test-writing-guidelines.md` anti-patterns (no self-referential simulations, no duplicates of existing core coverage).
10. Docs updated: `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` (cache evidence/diagnostics resolution) and `docs/dev/test-skill-reference.md` § "Legacy and foreign entries miss" so the dual-key lookup is documented where the cache contract lives.
11. Full suite passes.

## Key Files

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — `_cached_red_failures`, `_cached_red_evaluation`, `_resolve_audited_head`, the tree resolver from `SA-0MWIXIO0R006HL36`
- `skill/test_cache.py` — `FINGERPRINT_KIND_TREE`, `query_cached(fingerprint=…, fingerprint_kind=…)` (read-only, unchanged)
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `_resolve_commit_tree` / `_resolve_post_push_verification` precedent (`SA-0MWAXC5TD00461FN`)
- `skill/audit/tests/` — red-diagnostics cache test home (`test_audit_runner_green_run.py` or a sibling module)
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md`, `docs/dev/test-skill-reference.md`

## Dependencies

- Blocked by `SA-0MWIXIO0R006HL36` (core tree-first classifier query): it introduces the tree-resolution helper and `FINGERPRINT_KIND_TREE` wiring this item reuses rather than duplicating.

## Notes

- Root cause found while answering "does implement/audit run the full suite, and does push run it again?" — implement and the pre-push hook are correctly tree-keyed and de-duplicated; the audit is the remaining duplicate execution path.
- Do NOT weaken or remove the pre-push gate: it is the fail-closed proof that the pushed tree is the tested tree for pushes that bypass `finish`.
- This item deliberately does **not** change the classifier's green evidence path — that is `SA-0MWB1H4RF006R7SI`'s scope.

## Plan (2026-11-17)

Small item (effort `Small`, risk `Low`): planning pre-check returned `skip`, so no child decomposition. Six automated review stages ran against this content; AC coverage review returned `proceed`; stage advanced to `plan_complete`.

## Impact

A red dev-push gate verdict at the audited commit is visible to the audit's red diagnostics, so audits explain the failure from evidence the gate already produced instead of re-running the whole suite.

# Downtime workers commit directly to dev in the main checkout, breaking the pushed-tip invariant

## Problem statement

Twice during epic SA-0MWFJRWN00084FE1 the main checkout's `dev` carried **unpushed commits made directly in the main checkout** (not through a worktree `finish`), which made `implement.py start` refuse every new worktree with `Refusing to create a worktree from local dev: it is not a known pushed tip`. Recovery required publishing the foreign commits by hand, and the pre-push full-suite gate then `gate-refused` because the main checkout was dirty with a zero-content mode change (`100644 → 100755` on `skill/audit/scripts/persist_audit.py`).

The two observed commits were:

- `57768e2fe3` — `fix(machine-hygiene): remove shebang from config.py module (EXE001)` (no work-item id in the subject)
- `981af4d849` — `fix: Wrap implicit string concatenation in persist_audit.py (SA-0MWDKRD8G008Z164)` — landed by the herdr downtime worker for an item still `open`

## Root-cause verification (producer correction, 2026-11-18)

The producer's position — **the fix belongs in the skill layer, not the herdr dispatcher** — is correct on the substance, with one precision worth recording:

- The dispatcher is **not the committer**: `buildDowntimePaneArgs` only supplies `--cwd <main checkout root>`; it never runs `git commit`.
- The two observed commits are **ad-hoc agent commits**, not skill-helper commits. Both are authored `Sorra the Orc` and neither message is produced by any skill code path. The commit helpers that *can* commit are `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py::_commit_config_remediation` (message `audit: remediate ruff false positives (per-file-ignores)`) and `skill/code-review/scripts/linter_runner.py` / `skill/code_review/scripts/linter_runner.py::_commit_changes` (message `Auto-fix: <linter> applied fixes`).
- So the skill layer owns **both** the direct-commit helpers and the guardrails that should have stopped the ad-hoc commit. The dispatcher's `--cwd` is a contributing factor, not the defect.

Consequence for scope: option A (SorraAgents-only) is right, and AC3's **pre-commit hook** is the piece that catches ad-hoc agent commits — hardening the skill helpers alone would not have prevented either incident.

## Users

- **Herdr downtime dispatcher / downtime worker** — spawns `pi` panes with `--cwd <main checkout root>` and dispatches the `plan`, `intake`, `audit`, `implement` and `risk-effort` skills; a dispatched session that commits in that cwd poisons the shared `dev` ref for every other session.
- **Any implement session starting a worktree** — is blocked until the foreign commits are reconciled, regardless of which project or item it belongs to.
- **Producer / operator** — must currently reconcile by hand (inspect, verify, push or reset) with no attribution of which work item owns each foreign commit.

Example user stories:

- As an implement session, when I run `implement.py start`, I want a worktree created without first having to reconcile someone else's unpushed commits, so my work is never blocked by another session's shortcut.
- As a producer, when `start` refuses because `dev` is not a pushed tip, I want the refusal to name the work item(s) owning the unpushed commits, so reconciliation is one step instead of a manual log trawl.
- As the downtime worker, I want a dispatched session either to work in a worktree or to push what it commits before releasing the item, so the pushed-tip invariant is never broken by automation.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The committing skills (`audit` `_commit_config_remediation`; `code-review` and `code_review` `_commit_changes`) either work in a worktree, refuse to commit on `dev` in the main checkout, or push what they commit before releasing the item.
- `start`'s refusal names the owning work items of the unpushed commits (subject scan) so reconciliation is one step.
- A `.githooks/pre-commit` hook refuses a commit on `dev` in the main checkout at commit time (zero-width window — the commit is never created), with an explicit operator override for deliberate hot-fixes, and a `git_sandbox` test proves it fires in the main checkout and does not fire in a worktree or on a feature branch.
- A `scripts/reconcile-unpushed-dev.sh` helper lists the `origin/dev..dev` commits with their owning work items and offers push (default) or reset, and is documented in `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md`.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

One direct-on-dev commit from any session blocks worktree creation for every implement session in the repository until `dev` is reconciled; the higher the fan-out, the more often this recurs.

## Constraints

- **Worktree isolation.** SorraAgents implementation must happen in the worktree created by `implement.py start`; `finish` fails closed on writes outside it. The chosen scope (A) keeps every change inside a SorraAgents worktree.
- **Pushed-tip invariant.** `_resolve_start_base` (`skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`) deliberately refuses to branch from a local `dev` that is not a known pushed tip; that refusal must stay (it is the invariant, not the bug).
- **Fail-open on an unreachable remote.** A failed `git fetch` still branches from local `dev` (documented offline fallback) — the guard must not make offline work impossible.
- **No new blocking of legitimate finishes.** The post-push fast-forward of the main checkout's `dev` (SA-0MWFKDH78002T2CR) is a fast-forward, not a commit, so the pre-commit hook must not fire on it. `wl sync` commits on `refs/worklog/data`, not `dev`, so it is also unaffected.
- **Operator override.** A deliberate operator hot-fix on `dev` in the main checkout must remain possible via an explicit opt-in (e.g. `ALLOW_MAIN_CHECKOUT_DEV_COMMIT=1`), so the hook does not become an absolute prohibition.
- **UK English** in all written output.

## Existing state

- **The dispatcher runs panes in the main checkout.** `buildDowntimePaneArgs` forwards `--cwd <worklog root>` and `spawnAgentPane`/`spawnDowntimePane` spawn the pane there (`packages/ContextHub/packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.pane.ts`, `…/downtime-worker.dispatch-claims.ts`, `…/index.ts`). The dispatcher's skill kinds are `plan | intake | audit | implement | risk-effort`.
- **Skills that commit in their cwd.** `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py::_commit_config_remediation` (≈ line 14222) stages the config file and runs `git commit` **locally, no push**. `skill/code-review/scripts/linter_runner.py::_commit_changes` (≈ line 425) and a duplicate `skill/code_review/scripts/linter_runner.py::_commit_changes` (≈ line 641) run `git add .` + `git commit -m "Auto-fix: …"`.
- **`start` already refuses, but opaquely.** `_resolve_start_base` (`implement.py` ≈ line 8021) detects `local_dev_not_a_pushed_tip` and `phase_start` posts a comment (≈ line 12090) naming only the two tips and a three-step manual remedy — no attribution of the foreign commits to work items.
- **The pushed-tip guarantees are documented.** `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` (≈ line 2638) describes the three cooperating guarantees (pre-push deferral, post-push fast-forward, ancestry assertion) and the `_resolve_start_base` refusal.
- **A placement guard exists.** `implement.py` has implementation-placement gates (`SA-0MSGKAWXQ009VVG2`) and a read-only pre-claim foreign-mutation check of the main checkout, but they only cover sessions that go through the implement skill.
- **A dirty-checkout check exists.** `scripts/hygiene_check.sh::check_dirty_checkout` warns on a dirty main checkout, but it does not detect **committed-but-unpushed** `dev` commits.
- **A live-repo mutation guard exists.** `skill/shared/live_repo_guard.py` plus `tests/test_live_repo_mutation_guard.py` fail a test run that mutates a live ref — a candidate precedent for AC3's guard.
- **No pre-commit hook exists.** `.githooks/` ships `pre-push`, `pre-push.v2`, `post-checkout`, `post-merge`, `post-rewrite` and `worklog-post-pull`; `core.hooksPath` is `.githooks`, so a new executable `.githooks/pre-commit` is picked up automatically. `scripts/install_pi.sh` wires and refreshes the pre-push hook idempotently — the pre-commit hook needs the same treatment.

## Desired change

1. **Close the direct-commit path (skill side).** Harden `audit`'s and `code-review`/`code_review`'s commit helpers so they refuse (or redirect to a worktree, or push before release) when they would commit on `dev` in the main checkout.
2. **Attribute the refusal.** Parse the work-item ids out of the subjects of `origin/dev..dev` and include them in the `start` refusal message and its work-item comment, so reconciliation is one step.
3. **Add the immediate guard.** Add `.githooks/pre-commit` that refuses a commit on `dev` in the main checkout (with an operator override), wire it into `scripts/install_pi.sh`, and prove it with a `git_sandbox` test.
4. **Add the reconciliation helper.** Add `scripts/reconcile-unpushed-dev.sh` (list with owning items; push default, reset opt-in) and document it in `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md`.
5. **Record the dispatcher follow-up.** A ContentCreator/herdr dispatcher change (spawn in a worktree) is out of scope here and recorded as a linked follow-up — its worklog is not initialised (0-byte DB), mirroring the SA-0MWL51XNM001HMVC cross-repo precedent.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `_resolve_start_base` (≈ 8021) and the `phase_start` refusal comment (≈ 12090): add the unpushed-commit subject scan and name the owning work items.
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — `_commit_config_remediation` (≈ 14222): refuse/redirect/push when committing on `dev` in the main checkout.
- `skill/code-review/scripts/linter_runner.py` — `_commit_changes` (≈ 425) and `skill/code_review/scripts/linter_runner.py` (≈ 641): same guard (and reconcile the duplicate directory).
- `.githooks/pre-commit` — new pre-commit hook (main-checkout + `dev` detection, operator override).
- `scripts/install_pi.sh` — install/refresh the pre-commit hook idempotently, beside the existing pre-push wiring.
- `scripts/reconcile-unpushed-dev.sh` — new reconciliation helper (list + push/reset).
- `scripts/hygiene_check.sh` — `check_dirty_checkout` (≈ 179): optionally extend to unpushed-`dev` detection.
- `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` — reconciliation helper documentation (≈ 2638 section).
- `tests/` (e.g. `tests/test_pre_commit_main_checkout_guard.py`) — `git_sandbox` proofs for the hook and the `start` attribution.
- `packages/ContextHub/packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.pane.ts`, `…/downtime-worker.dispatch-claims.ts`, `…/index.ts` (ContentCreator) — **out of scope**, linked follow-up only.

## Related work

- **SA-0MW3H07A8004Q54C** — finish: retry the local-dev fast-forward after the recovery rebase and report a pushed-commit-guard refusal distinctly (completed). Same pushed-tip invariant family.
- **SA-0MVUTXJ4300301ZN** — Push to dev from the worktree that holds the commit (completed). Establishes that `finish` pushes from the checkout holding the commit.
- **SA-0MSGKAWXQ009VVG2** — Enforce git worktree usage for all implementation work (completed). Establishes the worktree requirement and the placement gate that this item extends to non-implement sessions.
- **SA-0MWFKDH78002T2CR** — deferred post-push fast-forward (referenced by the pushed-tip docs).
- **SA-0MWL51XNM001HMVC** — cross-repo hand-off precedent (herdr emitter filed in SorraAgents).
- Parent epic: **SA-0MWFJRWN00084FE1** (discovered from).

## Risks and assumptions

- **Ad-hoc-commit risk (medium).** The observed incidents were ad-hoc agent commits, not skill-helper commits, so the skill-helper hardening alone is insufficient — AC3's pre-commit hook is the necessary backstop. Both must land.
- **Guard false-positive risk (medium).** The pre-commit hook must not fire on the post-push fast-forward (not a commit), on `wl sync` (commits on `refs/worklog/data`), or in a worktree/feature branch. A `git_sandbox` test must pin each case.
- **Duplicate-directory risk (medium).** `skill/code-review/` and `skill/code_review/` both exist and both commit; only `code-review` has a `SKILL.md`. Fixing one and not the other would leave a live direct-commit path.
- **Operator hot-fix risk (medium).** An absolute prohibition on committing on `dev` in the main checkout would block legitimate operator hot-fixes; the explicit override keeps that path open.
- **Scope-creep risk (medium).** The dispatcher change (spawn in a worktree) is a ContentCreator concern; record it as a linked follow-up, not scope.
- **Assumption:** the "bounded window" for AC3 is **zero-width** — the pre-commit hook refuses the commit before it exists.
- **Assumption:** the reconciliation helper's default action is `push`; `reset --hard` requires explicit confirmation.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

**Q1 — Where does the fix live (scope split)?**
- Asked: The downtime dispatcher lives in ContentCreator (`packages/ContextHub/packages/herdr/`), but this item is filed in SorraAgents and AC2/AC4 are SorraAgents-side.
- Answer (producer, 2026-11-18): "I don't think you are correct, I believe it's in the skill not the dispatcher. Correct me if I'm wrong. In the meantime do A." → **Option (a) SorraAgents-only.** Verification: the producer is correct — the dispatcher never commits; the observed commits are ad-hoc agent commits and the skill layer owns both the commit helpers and the guardrails. The dispatcher `--cwd` is a contributing factor only, recorded as a linked ContentCreator follow-up.

**Q2 — What form does the AC3 guard take, and what is the "bounded window"?**
- Asked: pre-commit hook vs suite test vs hygiene-check extension.
- Answer (producer, 2026-11-18): "A" → **pre-commit hook** (`.githooks/pre-commit`) refusing a commit on `dev` in the main checkout, plus a `git_sandbox` test. Bounded window = **zero-width** (commit never created). Operator override retained for deliberate hot-fixes.

**Q3 — What is the "unpushed-commit reconciliation helper"?**
- Asked: documentation only vs script + documentation.
- Answer (producer, 2026-11-18): "B" → **script + documentation**: `scripts/reconcile-unpushed-dev.sh` (list `origin/dev..dev` with owning work items; push default, reset opt-in) documented in `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md`.

*All questions answered; intake complete.*

## Problem statement

`implement.py finish` builds once (Step 2), then pushes to `dev`. When the push
loses a race and is rejected non-fast-forward, `_recover_non_fast_forward_push`
fetches `origin/dev`, rebases the feature branch, recomputes the commit hash
and retries the push — **without rebuilding the worktree**. The pre-push hook
then runs the full suite against the rebased tree, where `packages/shared/dist`
(gitignored, produced by the build) is stale with respect to the `dev` commits
the rebase just pulled in. The gate goes red for a condition that does not
exist in a built tree, and the item's work is stranded until a human rebuilds.

## Users

- **Dispatch agent (leaf `finish` / driven child)** — "When my push loses a
  race to a sibling push, I want the retry to gate a tree I actually built, so
  my item lands instead of failing on a `TypeError` that names a function my
  own change set never touched."
- **Producer / operator on duty** — "I want a red dev-push gate to always mean
  something real about the pushed change set, so I never spend an hour and a
  half hand-rebuilding a worktree to clear a false red."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. After a successful recovery rebase inside the push loop, `finish` builds the
   rebased worktree **before** the retry push reaches the full-suite gate. A
   test simulates a non-fast-forward rejection whose rebase introduces a new
   `packages/shared` export and asserts (a) the build ran between the rebase and
   the retry push, and (b) the recorded push verdict is green/pushed.
2. A stale-dist failure is never attributed to the item's own change set. A
   test asserts that a gate failure whose symptom is a stale shared build
   (`TypeError: <new export> is not a function` — a runtime error that the
   existing load-flake retry does not match) cannot be reported as a failure of
   the pushed change set: either the run rebuilds first, or it fails closed with
   a build/resolution diagnosis naming the stale `packages/shared/dist`.
3. A genuine red introduced by the rebased commit is still reported red. A test
   pins that the rebuild does not weaken the gate: when the rebased tree really
   fails the suite, the push is blocked and the item stays `open`.
4. `finish` on a worktree whose push is rejected once still lands the commit and
   writes the terminal `completed` / `in_review` transition (no manual
   intervention).
5. A rebuild that itself fails after the rebase fails **closed**: no push, an
   actionable comment naming the build failure and the worktree, and the item is
   reset to `open` (mirroring the existing Step 2 build-failure path) — an
   unbuilt tree is never gated.
6. No extra build is paid when no rebase happened: the normal (uncontended) push
   path keeps exactly one build per `finish`, and the changed-scope gate
   (Step 3) is never re-entered by the retry loop.
7. Tests for every behaviour above are added to the `skill/implement` suite and
   pass, and the new tests fail against the pre-change implementation (no
   vacuous green).
8. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
   comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
9. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

A dispatch whose push races another push lands its work instead of spending an
hour and a half chasing a build-staleness false-red.

## Constraints

- Reuse the existing single build entry point `run_build(cwd)` so the rebuild
  inherits the current behaviour (disk-backed `TMPDIR` injection, 300 s timeout,
  no-build-script no-op for Python-only repos) — no parallel build code path.
- The rebuild runs **inside** the push retry loop, after the rebase and before
  the retry `git_push_to_dev` call; the Step 3 changed-scope gate and the
  "at most one full-suite gate per finish" property (SA-0MWFJS9OL001ZTTC) must
  survive.
- Never weaken the gate: a reproducible red on the rebuilt tree still blocks the
  push.
- Stay within the module's existing retry budget semantics
  (`DEFAULT_INFRA_RETRY_LIMIT = 5`): a rebuild failure is a hard stop, not a
  retryable transport condition.
- Worktree-only changes; no behaviour change for the main checkout.

## Existing state

- `_recover_non_fast_forward_push` (`skill/implement/scripts/implement.py:12262`)
  does: fetch `origin/dev` → `git rebase origin/dev` → capture the rewritten
  hash → `_assert_push_subject` → retry `git_push_to_dev`. There is no build
  step anywhere on this path.
- `run_build` (`implement.py:9324`) is the single build entry point; `phase_finish`
  Step 2 calls it once before tests (`implement.py:12763`).
- The pre-push gate (`.githooks/pre-push`) runs the full suite for `dev` pushes,
  bound to the pushed commit via `run_tests.py --gate-commit`, resolved by
  `resolve_gate_subject` (`skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py:3697`) — normally the
  worktree in place ("cheap in-place run"), so the suite executes against the
  worktree's filesystem including its `packages/shared/dist`.
- The verdict is tree-keyed (SA-0MW7C6BMZ00931JG) with change-set reuse
  (SA-0MWFJS9OL001ZTTC): a pure rebase is usually served from the pre-race
  verdict, so no suite runs. When the change set fingerprint **also** differs —
  e.g. the concurrently landed commit edited the same hub file the item edited
  (`packages/shared/src/predicates.ts` in the observed case) — the key misses,
  the suite really runs, and it runs on stale `dist`.
- Existing mitigation `_is_gate_load_flake` (`implement.py:6032`) retries once on
  suite *load* errors (`Cannot find package`, `Cannot find module`,
  `MODULE_NOT_FOUND`). A stale-dist runtime `TypeError` **loads fine** and falls
  outside those patterns, and retrying the identical unbuilt tree could not help
  anyway.
- `packages/shared/dist` is gitignored and produced by `npm run build`, so it is
  invisible to the tree fingerprint: two trees with identical git content can
  carry different `dist` contents. That is precisely the mismatch this item is
  about.
- Evidence (2026-11-18, ContextHub epic WL-0MWKE9VF800101V9, child
  WL-0MWKY141H002LULI): two consecutive false reds in one session — attempt 1
  rebased in `508a1821e` (`isNotStarted`) → 17 × `TypeError: isNotStarted is not
  a function`; attempt 2 rebased in `ac2a2c48e` (`normalizeStartOn`) → multiple
  `TypeError: normalizeStartOn is not a function`. Both cleared with no source
  change: `git fetch origin dev && git rebase origin/dev && npm run build` →
  `finish` green. Direct proof of staleness: `grep -c normalizeStartOn
  packages/shared/dist/predicates.js` → `0` before the manual build, `2` after.

## Desired change

The item offers three mechanisms; research picks one as primary and one as a
cheap hardening, and records why the third cannot fix the defect alone.

**A — Rebuild after a recovery rebase (recommended, primary).** After the
successful `git rebase origin/dev` in `_recover_non_fast_forward_push`, and
before the retry push, call `run_build(worktree_path)`. On failure, fail closed
(no retry push, failure comment naming the build stderr tail and the worktree,
item reset to `open`). Rationale: it makes the gate's subject and the build
consistent by construction, costs one build per rebase round (the rebase round
already costs a push attempt, and at most 5 rounds run), and needs no new
persistent state.

**B — Refuse to gate a tree newer than the last build (recommended hardening).**
Record the built tree SHA when the build succeeds (a `_set_finish_progress`
field / report field is enough — no new file format), and before a retry push
verify that `HEAD^{tree}` still matches it; when it does not, rebuild. This
generalises A to the other tree-changing paths that can precede a push (amend,
`git pull`, a rebase performed outside the recovery helper) at near-zero cost.
The fail-closed branch of the item's option 2 is therefore available as the
backstop without inventing a new abort source on the normal path.

**C — Rebuild-scoped cache key (rejected as a standalone fix).** The gate's key
is derived from the git tree (or the change-set patch), and `packages/shared/dist`
is gitignored, so a build-scoped key component could only be added by hashing a
build artifact into the key. That would invalidate verdicts for every unrelated
`finish` (every build produces a different `dist`), and it does not address the
actual defect: the suite *did* legitimately re-run, then failed on a stale
artifact. Keying cannot make an unbuilt tree built.

**Non-negotiable invariant (from the item):** whatever mechanism is implemented,
the push loop must never report a *source-level* test failure for a tree it did
not build.

## Key Files

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `_recover_non_fast_forward_push`
  (~12262) gains the post-rebase rebuild (A) / built-tree check (B); the push
  loop in `phase_finish` (~13560–13660) surfaces the rebuild in
  `report["steps"]["push"]`; `run_build` (~9324) reused unchanged;
  `_set_finish_progress` (~759) carries the built-tree marker for B.
- `skill/implement/tests/test_finish_push_robustness.py` — the existing
  non-fast-forward / load-flake harness (`_stubbed_finish`, `sandbox`) is the
  place for the AC1–AC5 tests.
- `skill/implement/tests/test_implement_push_retry.py` — drop-in coverage for the
  recovery helper if the rebuild is asserted at helper level rather than through
  `phase_finish`.
- `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` — the "A lost push race does not re-run
  the full suite" section (~2578) and the push-robustness list (~1715) need the
  post-rebase build documented alongside the change-set reuse they describe.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption:** the false red is caused by a stale build artifact, not by a
  wrong `dev` merge. The evidence (`isNotStarted` / `normalizeStartOn` in source
  but absent from `dist`, cleared by `npm run build` alone) supports this; if a
  similar red survives a rebuild, it is a genuine regression and must stay red
  (AC3).
- **Risk — rebuild churn vs. the push-subject guard.** On game repos `npm run
  build` runs `engine:sync` first, which can advance the engine submodule and
  stage the pin/gitlink. `_assert_push_subject` refuses a push from a worktree
  with tracked uncommitted changes, so a churn-producing rebuild could turn a
  recoverable race into a `PushSubjectMismatchError`. Mitigation: snapshot the
  churn baseline before the post-rebase build (reusing `_build_churn_baseline`),
  attribute the churn as finish's own like Step 2 does, and fail closed with an
  actionable comment when the churn cannot be carried.
- **Risk — cost.** One extra build per rebase round (≤ `DEFAULT_INFRA_RETRY_LIMIT`
  = 5 rounds). Accepted: it is far cheaper than the observed false-red recovery,
  and it is not paid on the uncontended path (AC6).
- **Risk — masking.** A rebuild that *hides* a real failure would be worse than
  the bug. Mitigated by AC3's pin test and by keeping the gate's verdict
  untouched: the rebuild changes what the suite measures, never the pass/fail
  threshold.
- **Scope-creep risk.** Making the full-suite cache key build-aware
  (mechanism C), hardening the load-flake pattern list, or re-running the suite
  after every rebase are **out of scope**; each is either rejected above or worth
  its own item. Any such finding during implementation is recorded as a linked
  work item (`discovered-from:SA-0MWMRHW01009Q22Q`), not absorbed here.

## Related work

- **SA-0MVPI41SR008JYXL** (completed) — "Hard-fail finish on stale shared
  resolution": covers the *resolution* check (worktree `@worklog/shared` →
  main checkout's `dist`) but not the rebase-then-gate-without-rebuild ordering.
- **SA-0MWFJS9OL001ZTTC** (completed) — "Stop rebase-induced full-suite re-runs on
  dev pushes": its change-set reuse usually hides this defect; this item covers
  the miss case (upstream touched the same file, so the patch's pre-images
  differ) and the invariant that survives reuse.
- **SA-0MW7C6BMZ00931JG** (completed) — "Gate keys on the pushed tree": the
  provenance contract the rebuild must make honest.
- **SA-0MW22SEMV00230O5** (completed) — push robustness; its AC7 load-flake retry
  is the nearest existing mitigation and is deliberately narrow (load errors
  only), which is why this defect slips through it.
- **SA-0MVMZBJGT00718ZO** (completed) — worktree link-farm / stale dist parent of
  the stale-resolution work.
- Discovered from ContextHub **WL-0MWKE9VF800101V9** (child WL-0MWKY141H002LULI);
  the two commits whose push triggered the rebases: ContextHub **WL-0MWKQ51G0006F3KV**,
  **WL-0MWMGEPY2004EDZ8**.

### Related work (automated `find-related` report)

- **SA-0MW3H07A8004Q54C** (completed) – finish: retry the local-dev fast-forward
  after the recovery rebase and report a pushed-commit-guard refusal distinctly
  — same recovery path, sibling concern (refs, not build artefacts).
- **SA-0MVUTXJ4300301ZN** (completed) – Push to dev from the worktree that holds
  the commit — the push subject this item's rebuild must keep honest.
- **SA-0MWHUVISS003APKM** (open) – Tests: fresh-worktree shared build
  precondition (red-first): makes `start` ensure a worktree's
  `packages/shared/dist` is built. Complementary, not overlapping: it fixes
  freshness at *start*, this item fixes freshness after a *mid-push rebase*.
  Interfaces with it through the shared build helper and its
  `shared_build` report block.
- Repository file matches: `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md`,
  `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`, `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions and answers

- **Q1: Which of the item's three mechanisms should the brief specify?**
  (Options: A rebuild-after-rebase; B record-the-built-tree / fail closed;
  C rebuild-scoped cache key.)
  **Recommended:** A as primary + B as hardening — A makes the gate's subject and
  the build consistent by construction for a bounded extra build per rebase
  round, B covers the other tree-changing paths cheaply; C alone cannot fix an
  unbuilt tree and would invalidate every unrelated verdict.
  **Answer (agent research, advisory until producer confirms):** A + B described
  in *Desired change*; C rejected with rationale. The acceptance criteria are
  written behaviourally (the item's invariant) so the producer can substitute B
  alone or A alone without rewriting them. Source: repo research —
  `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` (`_recover_non_fast_forward_push`,
  `run_build`, `_is_gate_load_flake`), `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py`
  (`resolve_gate_subject`), `skill/test_cache.py`
  (`compute_change_set_state`), `.githooks/pre-push`, and
  `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` § "A lost push race does not re-run the
  full suite".

## Goal

A recurring post-push verification refusal with `verdict=missing` (no full-suite cache entry for the pushed tree) is filed as a **critical `[test-failure]` item named "… — failing test"**, whose acceptance criteria no agent can satisfy, and every recurrence creates a *new* item because the triage dedupe only looks at critical items. Route such refusals as **gate/cache artefacts** and dedupe the signature **across priorities**.

## Root cause

1. **Mislabelling.** `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py::_post_push_failure_test_name()` falls back to `post-push full-suite verification: no valid full-suite cache entry` when no entry is `verdict=red`, and `_route_post_push_failure_to_triage()` files it through the triage helper exactly like a real regression. A cache miss therefore becomes a critical, agent-blocking "test failure" whose ACs ("the test … passes") cannot be met, and which only a human may close (false-positive rule in the runbook).
2. **Dedupe gap.** `skill/triage/scripts/check_or_create.py::list_critical_issues()` queries `wl list --priority critical --tags test-failure` only, so all three match heuristics are blind to an identical signature at any other priority. Evidence: the same signature already existed as `VC-0MWO58KVE000I7XZ` (commit `8169e29`, priority **high**) yet a second item, `VC-0MWOI6V8J000FHFL` (commit `af9370f`, critical), was created. The helper's documented "an existing matching critical `test-failure` item is enhanced instead of duplicated" contract consequently only holds among critical items.

## Producer decisions (2026-11-20)

- **Routing:** the fix lives in this repo (`SorraAgents`); the video_compiler item was a routing shell and was deleted after this item was filed.
- **Behaviour:** **keep the fail-closed refusal.** This item adds **no** self-heal and no finish-time suite runs; the cache-miss root cause remains with `SA-0MVXUCGPK003G2KV` (key the pre-push gate verdict on the pushed tree) and `SA-0MVCTZRZD004CE3L` (cache key ignores worktree/env identity).
- **Duplicate:** `VC-0MWO58KVE000I7XZ` was closed as a duplicate of this item.

## Scope (test-first ordering)

1. **Tests first** (`skill/triage/tests/`, `skill/implement/tests/`):
   - cross-priority signature match: an identical signature on a `high`-priority existing item is matched, a comment is added, and no second item is created;
   - gate-artefact routing: a `verdict=missing` refusal produces a gate-artefact title/tag with agent-satisfiable ACs;
   - regression guard: `verdict=red` still names the failing test from suite output and files a critical `[test-failure]` item.
2. `check_or_create.py`: match across all priorities (and by signature/commit), keeping "enhance, never duplicate"; record the recurrence as a comment on the existing item.
3. `implement.py`: name and route a `verdict=missing` refusal as a gate/cache artefact — distinct title prefix, tag, and ACs an agent can satisfy. The refusal itself stays fail-closed.
4. Runbook: add a "Gate/cache artefacts" subsection beside "Environmental failure signatures" in `skill/triage/resources/runbook-test-failure.md`, including the remediation (`run_tests.py --scope full`, then re-run `finish`).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A post-push `verdict=missing` refusal is filed with a gate-artefact title prefix and tag, never as `[test-failure] … — failing test`, and its acceptance criteria are satisfiable by an agent.
2. An identical failure signature matches regardless of the existing item's priority: a recurrence adds a comment to the existing item and creates no second item (regression test covers a `high`-priority existing item).
3. `verdict=red` routing is unchanged: a red entry still names the failing test from its output and files a critical `[test-failure]` item.
4. The triage runbook documents the gate/cache-artefact signature and its remediation.
5. The full project test suite passes.

## Impact

A cache-miss refusal stops masquerading as a critical test failure, so agents are no longer blocked by an item nobody can close and operators see one tracker per signature instead of one per commit.

- `skill/triage/tests/`

- `skill/implement/tests/`

- `list_critical_issues()` in `skill/triage/scripts/check_or_create.py` (near line 51).
