# Audit `--code-root`: model session cwd and cross-repo pre-flight still resolve against the worklog owner

**Discovered from:** WL-0MWTZEDWG008YMGQ (*Driven implement child sessions abort on a transient 'Provider finish_reason: error'*) — a cross-repo item tracked in the ContextHub worklog whose delivered code lives in this repository. Found during `/skill:audit WL-0MWTZEDWG008YMGQ` on 2026-11-25, alongside the already-tracked sibling SA-0MWQZGQVH003JWG1 (code-quality scan cwd).

## Problem statement

`--code-root <dir>` (LP-0MVZ6R5H8007NYLR) scopes the FILE SCOPE manifest, the merge gate, the changed-file list and the F3 execution worktree to the code repository, but it does **not** scope the two remaining cwd-sensitive surfaces. Both resolve against the audit process's launch cwd (the worklog owner's checkout), so a cross-repo audit produces **false blocking findings** even though the work is complete and merged.

**Defect 1 — model session cwd (false `unmet` ACs).** `_call_pi` spawns the Phase 1/Phase 2 session with `subprocess.Popen(cmd, stdout=..., stderr=..., env=pi_env)` — no `cwd=`. The session therefore runs in the launch checkout, and every relative path in the prompts (Key Files, touched files, FILE SCOPE manifest) resolves there. Observed: the Phase 1 screen returned `unmet` with the evidence *"test_spawn_failure_classification.py and test_drive_sibling_worktree_stray.py do not exist in ContextHub"* and *"docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md does not exist in ContextHub"*, when all three exist at HEAD in the code root (SorraAgents).

**Defect 2 — cross-repo pre-flight ignores an explicit code root (cross-repo child audits cannot run at all).** `_detect_cross_repo_scope_error` is called unconditionally at the start of Phase 1 (`if ctx.owning_root:` … `raise AuditScopeError(...)`), although its own docstring states *"Once the `--code-root` option lands, callers must skip this detection when an explicit code root is supplied."* A cross-repo **child** item (whose Key Files are all code-root-relative, with no worklog-owner path to fail open on) therefore aborts with `Error: Audit scope error: … No explicit code root was given` **despite** `--code-root` being passed — so the audit remediation path for such children is unavailable.

**Recovery cost.** The mis-scoped run demoted a completed item to `open`/`plan_complete`, set `needsProducerReview`, and required a second full audit (~7.5 min with a warm suite cache, ~28 min cold). Defect 2 made the targeted child re-audit impossible.

## Users

- **Producer/agent auditing a cross-repo item.** Story: *As an agent auditing an item whose code lives in another repository, I want `--code-root` to scope every cwd-sensitive surface, so a complete item is not failed on files the audit never looked at.*
- **Maintainer.** Story: *As a maintainer, I want the pre-flight guard to honour the explicit code root, so cross-repo child audits can be re-run to clear stale artefacts.*

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The audit model session runs with `cwd` set to the per-audit code root (the `--code-root` value when supplied, else the owning project root), so relative Key File / touched-file / manifest paths resolve in the code repository; a unit test pins the `cwd` passed to the spawn.
2. `_detect_cross_repo_scope_error` is skipped (or resolved against the explicit code root) when `--code-root` / `AUDIT_CODE_ROOT` is supplied, so a cross-repo child item with an explicit code root proceeds instead of raising `AuditScopeError`; a regression test pins the skip.
3. End-to-end evidence on a real cross-repo item: launching from the worklog owner's checkout with `--code-root <sibling>` yields no false `E902`/`unmet` findings and no `Audit scope error` — recorded on the work item.
4. Documentation (`docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md`) states that `--code-root` scopes the model-session cwd and the cross-repo pre-flight, and that launching from the worklog owner is supported for cross-repo items.
5. Full project test suite passes; changed-scope suite (`/skill:test`) passes before hand-off to review.

## Evidence (2026-11-25 run)

- Mis-scoped run (launched from `/home/rgardler/projects/ContextHub`, `--code-root /home/rgardler/projects/SorraAgents`): `~/.audit_debug/contexthub/WL-0MWTZEDWG008YMGQ-20261125-051751.log` — ACs 3 and 5 `unmet` ("do not exist in ContextHub"), 3 × high `E902` ruff findings on `/home/rgardler/projects/ContextHub/skill/implement/...`.
- Scoped re-run (identical flags, launched from `/home/rgardler/projects/SorraAgents`): `~/.audit_debug/sorraagents/WL-0MWTZEDWG008YMGQ-scoped-20261125-055002.log` — all 6 ACs `met`, `No code quality issues found.`, `Ready to close: Yes`.
- Child re-audit abort: `~/.audit_debug/sorraagents/WL-0MWU7BOVD000HL40-20261125-055837.log` — `Audit scope error … No explicit code root was given` although `--code-root` was passed.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — Defect 1: `_call_pi` subprocess spawn (line ~6861) needs `cwd=`; Defect 2: `_detect_cross_repo_scope_error` call site (line ~14969) needs code_root-aware skip.
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — `_detect_cross_repo_scope_error` function signature needs `code_root` parameter.
- `skill/audit/tests/` — New test files for Defect 1 (cwd pin) and Defect 2 (cross-repo skip).
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` — Update documentation for `--code-root` scoping.

## Related work

- LP-0MVZ6R5H8007NYLR — Original `--code-root` implementation that scoped some surfaces but missed these two.
- SA-0MWQZGQVH003JWG1 — Code-quality scan cwd (sibling defect already tracked).
- WL-0MWTZEDWG008YMGQ — The cross-repo item discovered by this audit (ContextHub worklog).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Scope-creep risk:** Other cwd-sensitive surfaces may exist beyond these two (e.g. other subprocess calls, config file resolution). Scope limited to Defects 1 and 2 confirmed by the evidence trail.
- **Assumption:** The `--code-root` resolution already returns the correct project root for cross-repo cases — verified in `_resolve_code_root` (line ~1028).
- **Assumption:** Same-repo audits (where launch_root == owning_root) are unaffected because cwd defaults to the current working directory, which is the launch directory — confirmed by the scoped re-run evidence.
- **Risk:** If `ctx` or the caller doesn't yet carry `code_root` at the Phase 1 entry point, the skip logic needs the resolved value threaded through. Verified: `_phase_gate` resolves it at line ~13202.

## Constraints

- `--code-root` must stay read-only and must not change the launch-context ownership verdict or any `wl` read/write path.
- A same-repo audit must be behaviourally unchanged (byte-identical verdict and manifest).

## Summary

`startOn` ("earliest instant the item may be worked on", WL-0MWM0FDZK007BAD0) is documented **nowhere** in this repo — `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md`, `Workflow.md`, `skill/`, `docs/` contain zero references to it — yet agents invent it as an ad-hoc "do not dispatch this yet" parking mechanism. Because `wl list` and `wl next` exclude future-dated items by default (visible only with `--include-not-started`), an invented hold silently hides the item from dispatch, and nothing ever clears it.

Clarify the rule: **`startOn` is only for real, time-based dependencies** — a date before which the work genuinely cannot proceed. It is not a parking lot for work that is merely unscheduled, and not a substitute for a dependency edge, a priority, or the `needsProducerReview` flag.

## Motivating example (RCA)

`CG-0MWR0BG9H007AFNU` — *Engine gap: scene-space guard over the episode manifest* (Tableau-Card-Engine, created 2026-11-21 by the `implement` session working its GDD engine-gap backlog):

- `startOn` was set to **2027-06-01** with the comment *"startOn is set past the GDD close so this item cannot dispatch before the build epic is scoped. Clear startOn when the build epic is created."*
- The clearing condition was satisfied **within days**: the build epic `CG-0MWNFVLYT003M7XF` and the backlog `CG-0MWPY2ECE002P2NH` both reached `in_review`/`completed`. The hold was nonetheless still set ~6 months later, so the item was invisible to `wl list` / `wl next` and would stay parked until 2027-06-01.
- Nothing surfaced it: the only reason anyone looked was an operator question ("why can't this start until 2027?"). Two later sessions (intake, `/plan`) force-claimed it with `--force-start-on <reason>` override comments instead of clearing the stale hold.
- The hold also gated nothing real: the plan's six child features carried no hold, and child 1 (`CG-0MWUOEDOW001SE94`) was `open`/`intake_complete` with a past `startOn` while its parent sat parked.

Net effect: a scheduling artefact that emitted no signal when its own precondition expired, and that a reader naturally misreads as a real 6-month dependency. The same pattern is latent in every repo that uses `wl`.

## Goal (user story)

As a producer reading a work item, I want `startOn` to be used only where a real time-based dependency exists and to be cleared the moment that dependency is satisfied, so that an item hidden from dispatch always means a genuine, still-live wait — never a forgotten parking note.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md` documents `startOn` as a first-class scheduling concept: its definition (earliest instant an item may be worked on, defaulting to `createdAt`), that future-dated items are excluded from `wl list` / `wl next` unless `--include-not-started` / `--starts-before` is passed, and how to clear it (`wl update <id> --start-on ""`).
2. The same section names the **only** legitimate uses — a real time-based dependency: an external event with a known date, a release/maintenance window, a dependent system's availability — with at least one worked example, and states that a *sequencing* dependency must be expressed with `wl dep` / `--parent` instead.
3. The same section names the **anti-patterns** explicitly: setting `startOn` to mean "not scheduled yet", "deprioritised", "waiting on another work item", "needs producer review", or "do not dispatch during this session" — with the correct mechanism given for each.
4. The clearing obligation is stated: a `startOn` hold must record its concrete clearing condition in a comment when set, and must be cleared (with a comment naming the satisfied condition) when that condition is met — a hold whose condition has been met is a defect, not a neutral state.
5. The skills that can set `startOn` (`skill/intake`, `skill/plan`, `skill/implement` and any shared helper that writes it) state that a session must not set `startOn` except for a real time-based dependency, and must record the clearing condition when it does; any existing call site that sets `startOn` for a non-time reason is corrected or removed.
6. `docs/dev/assignee-release.md` (or its successor) covers **both** hold mechanisms in one place — the `assignee` hold, `startOn`, and `needsProducerReview` as the only persistent hold — so a reader meets the whole "why is this item not dispatching?" model in one document, cross-linked from `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md`.
7. A machine check flags stale/long-dated holds: a repo-side check (script under `scripts/` and/or a worklog plugin under `.worklog/plugins/`) reports every item whose `startOn` is in the future and either (a) exceeds a configurable horizon (default 90 days) or (b) records no clearing condition, so a hold cannot rot invisibly again; the check's output names the id, title, `startOn` and the reason it was flagged.
8. The check is unit-tested against fixtures covering: a legitimate near-term hold, an over-horizon hold, a hold with no recorded clearing condition, and a cleared item (must not be flagged). Tests are written first (red) before the check.
9. The TCE RCA above is recorded in the documentation as the motivating case, with the item id and the dates, so the rule's justification is auditable rather than asserted.

## Constraints

- Must not break existing worklog CLI or data model — the policy is documentary + tooling.
- The machine check must be opt-in (wired into hygiene_check.sh) and must not fail the build if the worklog store is empty or inaccessible.
- Existing `startOn` values are grandfathered — the check reports but does not correct them automatically.

## Existing state

- `startOn` exists in the worklog CLI (`wl update --start-on`, `wl update --force-start-on`) with two worklog IDs (WL-0MWM0FDZK007BAD0, WL-0MWMGEUT10056MUI) but is undocumented in any agent-facing prose.
- No code paths in `skill/` write `start_on`.
- No items currently carry a future `startOn` value.
- `assignee-release.md` covers the assignee hold and `needsProducerReview` but not `startOn`.

## Desired change

1. Add a `startOn` policy section to `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md` beside the Assignee release invariant, with legitimate uses, anti-patterns, and clearing obligation.
2. Audit every code path that can write `start_on` — none exist in `skill/`, but verify and document the finding.
3. Add the stale-hold check (`scripts/check_start_on_holds.py` + tests), and wire it into `scripts/hygiene_check.sh`.
4. Cross-reference from `docs/dev/assignee-release.md` so both hold mechanisms live together.
5. Update the skills (`intake`, `plan`, `implement`) to document the rule.

## Implementation notes (added by `/plan`)

Routine research done while planning, recorded so the implement session does not re-derive it:

- **CLI behaviour confirmed:** `wl update --start-on <ISO-8601>` takes a full timestamp with an explicit timezone and `--start-on ""` clears the hold back to the item's `createdAt`; `--force-start-on <reason>` overrides the claim guard and records a comment. `wl list` / `wl next` exclude future-dated items unless `--include-not-started` or `--starts-before <iso>` is passed (from `wl update --help`, `wl list --help`).
- **AC5 audit result:** `grep -rn "start_on\|startOn\|start-on" skill/ docs/ AGENTS_GLOBAL.md` returns no hits, so no skill writes `start_on` today. AC5's "corrected or removed" branch is expected to be a no-op — re-verify at implementation and state the finding in the completion comment.
- **Clearing-condition marker (makes AC7(b) machine-checkable):** adopt the convention `startOn clearing condition: <text>` in a worklog comment at the moment a hold is set; `scripts/check_start_on_holds.py` flags a future hold whose comments carry no such marker (case-insensitive). The marker is the documentary form of AC4's clearing obligation, so policy and check share one spelling.
- **`scripts/hygiene_check.sh` integration shape:** the file is pure bash — each check is a `check_*` function printing one result line that may set `overall_exit`. Add `check_start_on_holds` in that shape, calling the new script; an empty, missing or inaccessible worklog store must report `skipped` and leave `overall_exit` untouched (fail-open, as `check_debris_worktrees` does).
- **`AGENTS_GLOBAL.md` link style:** repo-relative file links are rejected by `tests/test_agents_global_links.py` because the file installs as a symlink at `~/.pi/agent/AGENTS.md`; AC6's cross-link must be the absolute path `/home/rgardler/projects/SorraAgents/docs/dev/assignee-release.md`, matching the existing reference at the end of the Assignee release invariant section.
- **Test precedents to follow:** `tests/test_git_identity_guard.py` for a `scripts/check_*.py` unit-test layout, `tests/test_assignee_release_docs.py` for pinning the canonical hold-model wording.
- **Test-first ordering (AC8):** create `tests/test_check_start_on_holds.py` with the four fixtures (legitimate near-term hold, over-horizon hold, no clearing condition, cleared item) and confirm they fail before adding the script body.
- **Current store state:** zero items carry a future `startOn` today, so the check's first real run reports nothing — expected, not a defect.

## Verification

- `scripts/check_start_on_holds.py --json` emits one flag per stale hold naming the id, title, `startOn` and the reason it was flagged; exit 0 on an empty or unreadable store.
- `scripts/hygiene_check.sh` runs the new check and reports it in its summary without raising the exit code on an inaccessible store.
- The changed-scope test gate passes through `/skill:test` (covering `tests/test_check_start_on_holds.py`, `tests/test_agents_global_links.py`, `tests/test_assignee_release_docs.py`).

## Key Files

- `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md` — the policy statement (beside the Assignee release invariant).
- `docs/dev/assignee-release.md` — the combined hold model.
- `skill/intake/SKILL.md`, `skill/plan/SKILL.md`, `skill/implement/SKILL.md` — skill policy updates.
- `scripts/hygiene_check.sh` — wire in the new check.
- `scripts/check_start_on_holds.py` — new script.
- `tests/test_check_start_on_holds.py` — tests (TDD: tests first).

## Impact

A future-dated item always means a genuine wait, and a hold whose reason has expired is reported instead of hiding the work until its date arrives.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Routine:** Are any skills (`intake`, `plan`, `implement`) currently writing `start_on`? — **No.** Searched `skill/` for `start_on`, `startOn`, `--start-on`: zero hits (the only `start` hits are unrelated prose).
- **Routine:** Does `wl dep` cover every sequencing need? — **Yes.** `wl dep add`/`dep list`/`dep remove` provide explicit dependency edges for sequencing; the anti-pattern section redirects parking to these.
- **Routine:** Is a 90-day horizon reasonable? — **Yes.** The TCE case showed a hold rotting for ~6 months before discovery. 90 days is a reasonable window for a legitimate hold; the "no clearing condition" flag catches the edge case of very long legitimate holds.
- **Routine:** Should the check be a script or a worklog plugin? — **Script** under `scripts/` for simplicity, with a plugin option for future extension. The script follows the precedent of `check_git_identity.py` and is wired into `hygiene_check.sh`.
- **Routine (plan research):** Is AC7's "records no clearing condition" detectable without a convention? — **Needs a marker.** No existing comment format identifies a clearing condition, so `/plan` adopts the literal marker `startOn clearing condition:` (case-insensitive), documented in the policy section and detected by `scripts/check_start_on_holds.py`.
- **Routine (plan research):** Do relative links work in `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md`? — **No.** `tests/test_agents_global_links.py` forbids repo-relative file links because the file installs as `~/.pi/agent/AGENTS.md`, so AC6's cross-link is an absolute path.
- **Routine (plan research):** Does the store currently hold a future `startOn`? — **No.** `wl list --include-not-started --json` shows zero non-terminal items with `startOn` in the future.
- **Routine (plan research):** Is decomposition into child work items warranted? — **No.** A single Small-effort, Medium-risk docs+tooling change with 9 measurable ACs, a five-point desired-change list and named key files; one worktree session delivers the vertical slice (policy text, doc cross-link, script, tests, hygiene wiring). Test-first ordering is pinned inside AC8 and the implementation notes rather than separate child items.

## Plan: changelog

- 2026-11-26T21:12:16Z — `/skill:plan` reviewed the existing content instead of decomposing it: verified AC1–AC9 trace to the Summary / Desired change / RCA, validated the `**Key Files:**` section, added the Implementation notes and Verification sections, extended the Appendix with plan-time research, ran the six automated review stages and the AC coverage review, and advanced stage `intake_complete` → `plan_complete`. No child work items created; the intake-time effort/risk estimate (Small / Medium, 7.27 h recommended) still applies because scope is unchanged.

# `audit_runner.py issue <id>` must audit that item only — never drain the host-wide audit queue

## Problem statement

A single-item audit (`audit_runner.py issue <id>`, including the ship release gate's `issue <id> --strict --ship-triggered` remediation call) silently continues into a **global, host-wide batch drain** after the primary audit succeeds: when the shared `audit-batch` priority queue holds ≥ 2 entries — which may all belong to *other* projects — the same process audits up to 5 foreign work items within the same 30-minute window. This inflates a one-item audit to tens of minutes (48 min observed), consumes the release gate's remediation budget, and has been observed surfacing another project's acceptance criteria and variance rows inside a SorraAgents item's persisted Phase-2 report — a contamination path that could produce a false "Ready to close: Yes" at the release gate.

## Users

- **Release engineer / ship skill operator**: runs `audit_runner.py issue <id> --strict --ship-triggered` as a bounded gate remediation and needs it to finish within the 29-minute per-item budget, auditing exactly the item under gate.
- **Agent implementing a work item**: runs the audit skill on its own item and expects the verdict to describe *that* item's evidence only.
- **Downtime/audit dispatcher (herdr)**: needs a single, explicit entry point that drains the machine-wide queue across projects.

Example user stories:

- As a release engineer, when the gate re-audits item X, the run takes as long as auditing X takes and never audits items from another repository, so the remediation budget is spent on the blocker.
- As an implementing agent, I can trust that a "Yes" verdict persisted on my item was derived from my item's acceptance criteria and repository evidence, not another project's.
- As the audit dispatcher, I can still ask for one drain window across all projects by running `audit_runner.py batch` explicitly.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `audit_runner.py issue <id>` audits **only** `<id>` (and, unchanged, its children): with two or more foreign entries queued in the `audit-batch` queue, a single-item run audits none of them, leaves every entry queued, and its exit code and persisted verdict are unaffected by their presence.
- The post-audit drain is **explicit** for `issue`: it runs only when the operator passes `--batch-drain`; neither the default invocation nor `AUDIT_BATCH_DRAIN` (which no longer switches the drain on) can trigger it, while `AUDIT_BATCH_DRAIN=0` still disables an explicitly requested drain.
- An explicitly requested `issue --batch-drain` drains only entries whose stamped owning project root matches the audited item's owning root; entries owned by other projects, and legacy entries with no stamped root, remain queued untouched and are reported as skipped in the batch metrics line.
- `audit_runner.py batch` remains the single explicit cross-project drain entry point: its priming, per-item worklog routing (each item audited against its own project's `.worklog`), priority/FIFO order, and wall-clock budget are unchanged.
- A regression test proves report isolation: a run started for a SorraAgents item that sees a foreign queued entry produces no persisted audit and no `wl` write for the foreign entry, and a persisted report's acceptance-criteria and variance rows derive only from the audited item's (and its children's) own worklog data.
- `skill/audit/SKILL.md` (batch-drain paragraph), `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` (batch-drain activation/queueing/configuration sections), the `--batch-drain`/`--no-batch-drain` help text and the `cmd_issue` docstring are updated to state that `issue` is single-item by default and `batch` is the cross-project drain.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

A single-item audit now finishes auditing that item and stops, so a release-gate remediation or an agent's own audit can no longer be hijacked by another project's queued work and can no longer report another project's evidence under this item's name.

## Constraints

- Keep the `batch` subcommand's cross-project dispatch intact (LP-0MW96A9GW009KVF7 AC3): do **not** partition the queue by project or rename the queue — a dispatcher must still be able to drain all projects in one explicit window.
- Skipped entries must never be dropped: foreign and legacy entries stay in the queue for their own project's drain, and repeated runs must leave the queue byte-for-byte equivalent (idempotent).
- Children of the audited item remain in scope exactly as today (child audits, `--audit-children` cascade, in-main-slot child screens are unaffected).
- Any `skill/shared/queue.py` change must be additive and backward compatible — the queue is used by other skills and by tests.
- Release gate bounds must be respected: `SHIP_AUDIT_REMEDIATION_TIMEOUT_MS` (29 min per item) must no longer be consumed by foreign work.
- Behaviour change is documented loudly because operators may currently rely on the implicit drain (the documented migration path is `audit_runner.py batch`).

## Existing state

- `cmd_issue` ends with `if rc == 0 and batch_drain is not False: if _batch_drain_enabled(): _maybe_run_batch_drain(ctx)` (`skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`, ~18681). `batch_drain=None` (the CLI default) therefore resolves to ON, and `_batch_drain_enabled()` returns True unless `AUDIT_BATCH_DRAIN=0` (~5722).
- `_maybe_run_batch_drain` gates on the **global** queue depth (`PriorityQueue("audit-batch")`, `_batch_drain_should_run(len(queue))`, ≥ 2 entries) with no project scoping (~18690).
- `_batch_drain_cycle` dequeues strictly by priority/timestamp, skips only `audit:` tickets, the caller's own id and duplicates; the entry's `project_root` is passed to the audit callback for worklog routing, but foreign entries are audited regardless (~5839).
- `_batch_audit_one` re-runs the full `cmd_issue` pipeline for each drained item against `<project_root>/.worklog` and with `batch_drain=False` (~18712).
- The queue is host-wide (`$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/pi-semaphores/audit-batch`) and shared by every project on the machine (`skill/shared/queue.py::PriorityQueue`).
- The ship skill's gate remediation calls `audit_runner.py issue <id> --strict --ship-triggered` (`skill/ship/scripts/check-audit-gate.js`, `check-final-validation.js`, `refresh-audits.js`) with no `--no-batch-drain`, so a gate run inherits the global drain.
- Observed evidence (from the item report): repeated `Warning: audit launched from /home/rgardler/projects/SorraAgents but work item RISE-… is owned by /home/rgardler/projects/tce-the-rising` lines inside an SA-item run, `Audit slot acquired: … ticket=audit:RISE-…` in the same run, and one single-item audit lasting 48 minutes (10:58 → 11:46).
- The `--batch-drain` / `--no-batch-drain` CLI flags exist but the default (auto) path is what fires; `AUDIT_BATCH_DRAIN` is documented as an opt-out, not an opt-in (~19288).

## Desired change

1. Resolve the `issue` drain default to **off**: `batch_drain=None` means "do not drain"; only an explicit `--batch-drain` opts in for that run. Keep `AUDIT_BATCH_DRAIN=0` as a hard disable of any requested drain and drop its "auto-on" meaning (document the change).
2. Scope any explicit `issue`-run drain to the audited item's owning project root: entries whose stamped `project_root` differs — and legacy entries with no stamped root — are left in the queue and counted in the metrics line (e.g. `skipped_foreign=N`, `skipped_unattributed=M`). Implement via an additive filtered-next helper in `skill/shared/queue.py` (or an internal peek/remove loop that never drops an entry).
3. Keep `cmd_batch` (the `batch` subcommand) unchanged as the explicit cross-project drain, and keep `_batch_audit_one`'s per-item worklog routing.
4. Add regression tests in `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_batch_drain.py`: (a) `cmd_issue` does not invoke `_maybe_run_batch_drain` with the default invocation; (b) a `--batch-drain` run with mixed SA-/foreign queue entries audits only the SA- ones and leaves the foreign entries queued; (c) legacy rootless entries are skipped, not audited; (d) an `Audit batch drain:` line reports the skips. Add a report-isolation test (see AC5) in the same suite or the adjacent `cmd_issue` trigger tests.
5. # In-main-slot child verdicts cannot be persisted by a session

## Problem statement

The documented in-main-slot resume cycle — "perform each emitted `[AUDIT_IN_MAIN_SLOT_WORK]` screen, persist the child audit, then re-run the parent to collect the verdicts" — cannot be completed when the session persists the child verdict with `wl audit-set --audit-file <report>`. The parent re-run both **rejects** the text verdict (it is not accepted by the reuse path) and **clobbers** it by persisting a fresh `partial — main-session review` placeholder over it. A session that follows the documented contract therefore livelocks: only a lucky single run (parent screen + child screen in the same invocation) can pass.

## Users

- **Producer/Agent running a parent audit**: services the emitted child screens and expects the persisted verdicts to stick and be collected on the next parent run.
- **Herdr/downtime workers**: automate the audit loop; a livelock burns LLM slots and never converges.
- **Release reviewer (ship gate)**: blocks the release because the parent audit can never report `Ready to close: Yes` while a serviced child is re-screened and reset to pending.

Example user stories:

- As an agent servicing an in-main-slot child screen, I want the verdict I persist (via the documented command) to be reused by the parent with zero child `pi` calls, so that the parent converges after one servicing pass.
- As a release reviewer, I want a re-run of the parent audit to honour an already-serviced, fresh child audit instead of overwriting it with a pending placeholder.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Session-persisted verdicts are reused.** After a session services an emitted `[AUDIT_IN_MAIN_SLOT_WORK]` screen and persists the child verdict with the documented command (including a `wl audit-set --audit-file <report>` text report carrying a `Ready to close: Yes` line and a per-AC table), a subsequent parent audit collects that child with **zero** child-screening `pi` calls, records the `reused_from` / `child_audit_ready` markers, and emits no `[AUDIT_IN_MAIN_SLOT_WORK]` screen for it. This holds for a **gap-mapped** child (parent has gaps and the child owns the gap files) as well as for a child collected by the Phase 1 child-verdict pre-pass.
- **AC2 — A serviced child audit is never clobbered.** A parent re-run must never persist a pending (`partial` + `main-session review`) child report over a stored child audit that is fresh and carries a real, non-pending verdict and AC table — whether that audit was persisted by the runner or by a session via `wl audit-set --audit-file`. The serviced report (verdict + AC table) survives the parent run.
- **AC3 — Documented persist path is exact.** The audit skill and reference document the exact command a session must use to persist a serviced in-main-slot child screen so that reuse accepts it, and the emitted `[AUDIT_IN_MAIN_SLOT_WORK]` payload / `Child screens pending` instruction points to that command. Following **only** the documented steps converges the cycle (no re-emitted screens, no `unserviced_in_main_slot` classification for serviced children).
- **AC4 — Convergence end to end.** After servicing all emitted screens and re-running the parent, the `Child screens pending` gate clears, `pending_child_screens` is empty, the `<id>.pending-screens.json` signal is removed, and the parent report names only genuine remaining parent AC gaps.
- **AC5 — Regression tests.** Unit tests cover: (a) a session-persisted, fingerprint-less `wl audit-set` report (`Ready to close: Yes` + AC table) is reused by the gap-mapped path with zero child screens; (b) the persist-overwrite guard skips a pending child report over such a serviced audit; (c) the documented persist command produces a report the reuse path accepts. No real `pi` or `audit_runner` subprocess is invoked.
- **AC6 — Documentation.** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, `skill/audit/SKILL.md`, `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md`, and any relevant resume-cycle references.
- **AC7 — Full project test suite.** Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

A session can now service an in-main-slot child screen once — persisting the verdict makes it stick, and the next parent run collects it instead of re-screening and clobbering it — so parent audits on epics with gap-mapped children converge instead of livelocking.

## Constraints

- **Do not weaken the strict v2 content-freshness gate** for runner-persisted child audits; the new acceptance of session-persisted reports is additive (a fallback), not a relaxation of the fingerprint contract for reports that carry one.
- **`--force` still bypasses reuse** — every child is re-audited under `--force`; the new path must not change that.
- **Lifecycle neutrality is preserved** — a parent-persisted child audit must still never change the child's lifecycle (the existing `_restore_child_pre_audit_lifecycle` contract).
- **No new `wl` schema or CLI field** unless an existing documented option (e.g. `wl audit-set --fingerprint`) is used; any helper must live in the audit runner/skill.
- **The separate-process mode (`--no-child-in-main-slot`) is unchanged.**
- **Scope-creep risk**: general audit-report parsing improvements, cross-repo consumer ACs (e.g. `LP-0MVOBJGB4001TQ8X`), and unrelated freshness-gate work are out of scope and must be recorded as linked work items rather than folded in.

## Existing state

The residual defect is confined to the paths that require a **v2 content fingerprint**, which a session-written `wl audit-set` report never carries:

- **Gap-mapped re-screen** — `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py::_phase_children`, parent-first gap-mapped branch (~line 16661): it calls `_get_child_content_fresh_verdict` (~line 9757), which returns `(None, None)` for a fingerprint-less report by design. The child is added to `pending_children` and its `[AUDIT_IN_MAIN_SLOT_WORK]` screen is re-emitted.
- **Persist-overwrite guard** — same function, child-persist loop (~line 16809): it skips persisting only when `_get_child_content_fresh_verdict(...)[0] is not None`, i.e. only for a v2 content-fresh audit. A session-persisted report is not content-fresh, so the pending placeholder is persisted over it (the clobber).
- **Underspecified persist step** — the emitted `[AUDIT_IN_MAIN_SLOT_WORK]` payload (`_emit_in_main_slot_work`, ~line 6513; prompt built in `_phase1_review_child_acs`, ~line 10106) is a READ-ONLY screen prompt and never names a persist command. The `Child screens pending` gate (`_assemble_child_audit_report`, ~line 8597) and the pending-screens signal instructions (`_write_pending_screens_signal`, ~line 8118) say only "persist the child audit". The session reasonably chooses `wl audit-set --audit-file <report>`, which stores the text but no v2 fingerprint line.
- **Why the Phase 1 pre-pass is not the blocker** — the non-gap Phase 1 pre-pass (~line 16095) uses `_get_child_audit_verdict` (~line 9623), which does accept fingerprint-less reports through the legacy time-gate floor when `auditedAt` is fresh. The reproduction hit the gap-mapped branch, which is strictly content-fingerprint-gated. The clobber, however, can poison the time gate on later runs by bumping the child's `updatedAt`.

Reproduction evidence (v0.2.0 release review, 2026-11-25, parent `SA-0MWFFX49M0016KOK`): three children (`SA-0MWFFXNNM00148IX`, `SA-0MWFFXKKA005CLVK`, `SA-0MWFFXQNT002LB8T`) were serviced and persisted with `wl audit-set --audit-file`; all showed `readyToClose=true`; the next parent run re-emitted the screens, overwrote the verdicts with `partial — main-session review`, and classified all three `[unserviced_in_main_slot]`.

## Desired change

Make the documented resume cycle work end to end for a session-persisted child audit, without weakening the v2 gate for runner-persisted audits. Any of the item's originally proposed directions is acceptable; the preferred combination is:

1. **Accept a session-persisted verdict on the reuse path (fallback).** When no v2 fingerprint is present, fall back to the legacy time-gated verdict acceptance (`_get_child_audit_verdict` semantics) for the gap-mapped branch, so a fresh `wl audit-set` report with a parseable `Ready to close:` line and AC table is collected with zero child `pi` calls. Use the same fallback in the checkpoint-resume re-resolution if it is reachable there.
2. **Guard the persist overwrite.** Broaden the persist-overwrite guard so a pending child report is never persisted over **any** fresh stored child audit carrying a real non-pending verdict, not only a v2 content-fresh one. Keep `--force` and the runner-persisted reuse markers authoritative.
3. **Document the exact persist command.** Either document the existing `wl audit-set` invocation (and, if it is sufficient, the `--fingerprint` value the session must pass) or add a small runner helper that assembles/persists the report with the v2 fingerprint line. Embed the exact command in the emitted screen payload and the pending-screens instruction so following the docs alone converges.
4. **Regression-test the three behaviours** in AC5 with fixtures that model a session-written fingerprint-less report (no real subprocess).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — `_phase_children` gap-mapped branch (~16661) and child-persist guard (~16809); `_get_child_content_fresh_verdict` (~9757); `_get_child_audit_verdict` (~9623); `_child_acs_from_own_audit` (~9860); `_emit_in_main_slot_work` (~6513); `_phase1_review_child_acs` (~10106); `_write_pending_screens_signal` (~8118); `_assemble_child_audit_report` gate (~8597).
- `skill/audit/SKILL.md` — in-main-slot resume-cycle section (~227–241).
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` — resume-cycle composition (~1293–1305) and child-verdict reuse (~1418).
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_child_in_main_slot.py` — end-to-end resume tests (`TestResumeCycleEndToEnd`).
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_freshness.py` — freshness / reuse tests.
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_child_persist_demotion.py` — persist guard tests.

## Related work

- `SA-0MWFFX49M0016KOK` — source item (discovered-from); its 2026-11-25 comment records the full clobber sequence.
- `SA-0MVZ3SMK6007431I` — partial-overlap predecessor: gap-mapped reuse + persist-overwrite guard, scoped to **content-fresh (v2)** audits only; it deliberately leaves fingerprint-less audits re-screened. This item is the residual gap.
- `SA-0MSQJA0WL006UJ3T` — child verdict reuse (LP-0MSQ32MF200675AR) foundation.
- `SA-0MSQJABHZ0018APE` — content-gate child verdict reuse in parent audits.
- `SA-0MVSTZ71J001P67S` / `SA-0MW2J7O3D0044SFM` — in-main-slot resume + checkpoint re-resolution (the resume cycle this bug breaks).
- `SA-0MVAWFUU0004VW45` / `SA-0MVAWFYZE0040SQ3` — unserviced in-main-slot assessment and reason diagnostics (reporting side; this item is the persistence side).
- `SA-0MVTU2643004QTQN` — content-freshness contract docs.
- `SA-0MVAWFPVU001E1T0` — unserviced in-main-slot verdict tests.
- `SA-0MWIXJ84T000GBWG` — fingerprint_kind/age reporting when a cached verdict is reused (related, blocked).

Potentially related docs:

- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` (resume-cycle composition, freshness gate, child-verdict reuse).
- `skill/audit/SKILL.md` (in-main-slot mode, child-audit execution contract).
- `docs/dev/audit-reliability-rca.md`, `docs/dev/audit-child-demotion-rca.md` (prior cliff/loop analyses).


## Plan: changelog

- **2026-11-26** — Plan skill decomposed this item into five children (test-first ordering): red-first regression tests → reuse path → persist guard → documented persist command → end-to-end convergence. Dependencies: the test task first; *Reuse* depends on it; *Never clobber* depends on both; *Document* depends on *Reuse*; *Verify convergence* depends on all implementation children. Effort re-estimated (Small / Medium, recommended 14.5 h, confidence 85%). Key research finding recorded in the Appendix: `wl audit-set` stores a schema-2 fingerprint in the audit record that the reuse gate never reads, and the legacy time gate cannot converge once a post-persist comment moves `updatedAt`. AC coverage review: `proceed` (all seven parent ACs covered by child criteria).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q: Which of the three proposed remediation directions (a: accept `wl audit-set` text verdicts; b: provide a documented persist command; c: honour an already-fresh stored child audit on re-run) should be implemented?**
  - **Answer (agent, documented assumption):** Implement the preferred combination in *Desired change* — (a)+(c) in the runner plus (b) in the documentation/emitted instruction. Rationale: the source item explicitly accepts any of the three; this combination removes the livelock end to end and keeps the v2 gate intact for runner-persisted audits. Evidence: source description ("Expected: Either (a) … or (b) … or (c)") and the 2026-11-25 comment on `SA-0MWFFX49M0016KOK`. This is a design assumption, not an open producer question; the plan/implement stages may refine the mechanism.
- **Q: Does `wl audit-set` guarantee `updatedAt == auditedAt`, so the legacy time-gate fallback can accept a fingerprint-less session report?**
  - **Answer (research):** The audit docs state that the atomic `wl audit-set --ready-to-close yes` path sets `updatedAt = auditedAt` (`skill/audit/SKILL.md` line 49; `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md`). Implementation must verify this holds for `--audit-file` too and, if not, either use the report's own audited timestamp or add a fingerprint to the persisted report. Source: repo docs.
- **Q: Is this a duplicate of `SA-0MVZ3SMK6007431I`?**
  - **Answer (research):** No full duplicate. That item's AC1/AC2 are explicitly scoped to content-fresh (v2-fingerprinted) audits and leave fingerprint-less audits re-screened; this item covers the session-persisted `wl audit-set` text-verdict case that the predecessor left open. Recorded as a duplicate-check comment on this item. Source: `SA-0MVZ3SMK6007431I` description + code comments at `audit_runner.py` ~16661/16809.
- **Q: Is the clobber also reachable via the non-gap Phase 1 pre-pass?**
  - **Answer (research):** The non-gap pre-pass uses `_get_child_audit_verdict` (time-gate fallback) and so can accept a fresh fingerprint-less report; the reproduction hit the gap-mapped branch, which is strictly content-fingerprint-gated. The clobber guard is shared, so the fix must cover both branches for consistency. Source: `audit_runner.py` ~16095, ~16661, ~16809.

- **Q: Is the legacy time-gated fallback (direction 1 in *Desired change*) sufficient to converge the 2026-11-25 reproduction?**
  - **Answer (research, measured 2026-11-26):** No. `wl audit-set --audit-file` sets `workitems.updatedAt = auditedAt` (`worklog dist/persistent-store.js::saveAuditResult`), but the reproduction child `SA-0MWFFXNNM00148IX` shows `auditedAt = 2026-11-25T17:21:08Z` against `updatedAt = 2026-11-25T22:34:46Z` — a later comment pushed `updatedAt` five hours past the audit, so `_audit_time_is_fresh` is false and the 30 s write-delta tolerance does not apply. A time-gate-only fallback would still classify the serviced report stale. The plan therefore makes the **audit-record fingerprint** the primary acceptance path and keeps the time gate as a compatibility floor. This supersedes the earlier Appendix answer that assumed the time gate would carry it.
- **Q: Does `wl audit-set` store a content fingerprint the runner can read, and is it identical to the runner's schema-2 fingerprint?**
  - **Answer (research, measured 2026-11-26):** Yes. `wl audit-set` resolves the fingerprint as `--fingerprint` → an embedded `Audit content fingerprint:` line → `computeContentFingerprint({title, description})` (WL-0MVK01BBD005V7KK) and stores it in the audit record's `fingerprint` column; `wl audit-show --json` returns it. For `SA-0MWFFXNNM00148IX` the stored value `a37400a8e047a38432001f6f652a067211023317bc094147877ab82720cbf11d` equals `audit_runner._compute_content_fingerprint` for the same item, while `_extract_content_fingerprint(rawOutput)` is `None` — i.e. the fingerprint exists but the reuse gate never looks at it. This is the root cause and the primary remediation: read `audit.fingerprint` when the report text carries no embedded line.
- **Q: Is a new `wl` CLI field or a runner persist helper required (direction 3 in *Desired change*)?**
  - **Answer (research):** No. The existing `wl audit-set <child> --ready-to-close <yes|no> --audit-file <report>` invocation already stores a schema-2 fingerprint and sets `updatedAt = auditedAt`, so documenting that exact command (and surfacing it as a `persist_command` field in the emitted `[AUDIT_IN_MAIN_SLOT_WORK]` payload) is sufficient once the reuse gate reads the record fingerprint. A helper CLI was rejected under the item's "no new `wl` schema or CLI field" constraint and the Simplicity First discipline. Recorded as a design assumption; the implementation may revisit only if the documented command proves insufficient.
- **Q: Which persist ordering should the documentation recommend?**
  - **Answer (research):** Persisting the child audit **after** any comments/status changes on the child remains the recommended ordering (it keeps the legacy time gate satisfied for older `wl` versions), but it is no longer required for convergence because reuse reads the stored fingerprint. The documentation states both.

SorraAgents skills recover a work item's acceptance criteria by regexing the
`## Acceptance Criteria` section out of the work item's `description` (canonical
implementation: `skill/shared/tree_coverage.py::extract_acceptance_criteria`).
Worklog is adding a first-class `acceptance_criteria` table with one row per
criterion — stable id, ordering, text, status (`met|unmet|partial|modified`)
and, for `modified` rows, the original text plus the justification. Skills must
switch from prose parsing to the table so a criterion has identity and status.

## Users

- **Pi agent sessions** that run skills consuming acceptance criteria programmatically: `audit`, `implement`, `find-related`, `plan`, `intake`, `report`.
- **Developer** maintaining those skills — needs predictable, testable AC behaviour regardless of description edits.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Every skill that extracts acceptance criteria programmatically reads them from
  the worklog table (`wl ac show <id> --json`) instead of parsing description
  text; `skill/shared/tree_coverage.py::extract_acceptance_criteria` either
  delegates to the table or remains only as an explicit legacy/description
  fallback, with the fallback documented and tested.
- `find-related` and `implement` are updated first (as named in the parent
  request) to use the AC rows rather than a full `wl show` where the table
  suffices.
- AC-coverage review (`skill/shared/tree_coverage.py::compute_coverage` /
  `apply_coverage_review`) compares criteria rows — by id where both sides are
  migrated, by similarity only for unmigrated descriptions — and its behaviour
  is covered by tests.
- Per-criterion status is honoured where the skills already reason about
  criteria (audit reports, plan coverage, intake briefs): a `met` criterion does
  not count as a gap, and a `modified` criterion is shown with its original text
  and justification.
- Skills remain functional against a store that has **not** yet run `wl doctor
  upgrade` (no AC rows): the fallback path is exercised by a test.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
  comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

Agents stop re-parsing acceptance criteria out of prose and read them as
